suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'bucket squatting'—attacker-created buckets mimicking legitimate model upload destinations. Pipeline missed IOC extraction and detection for CreateBucket API calls with names matching project naming patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GCS CreateBucket operations where bucket name closely resembles existing Vertex AI project IDs or follows '{project}-{stage}-models' patterns. Trigger if creator is external service account, uses residential IP, or precedes model upload attempts by <12 hours.

suggestion.title: Vertex AI Model Upload Redirected to Non-Approved GCS Bucket
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'hijack model uploads'—SDK redirects or accepts model writes to attacker-controlled buckets. Pipeline failed to surface model upload interception or unauthorized bucket-destination writes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect aiplatform.models.upload or datasets.upload operations that resolve GCS target to buckets outside approved project storage locations. Cross-correlate: if bucket created <24h prior by different principal, flag as model hijacking attempt.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Vertex AI SDK Version Usage with Unauthorized Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Headline specifies 'SDK flaw'—implies specific vulnerable versions. Pipeline extracted zero version IOCs and no execution-phase detection for compromised SDK loads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for google-cloud-aiplatform package versions <[min_patched_version] loading in production environments. Correlate with unexpected GCP authentication events (new service accounts) or model-upload API calls initiated from unusual processes.

suggestion.title: Cross-Project Service Account Token Used for GCS Bucket Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must credential-hop to squatted buckets; pipeline missed detection of service account token misuse or out-of-project IAM role assumption around model operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect service account credentials (OAuth2 tokens) performing model.upload or bucket.putObject from projects other than where the credentials were created. Alert if token used by Vertex AI SDK service account suddenly grants storage.buckets permissions to buckets with squatting-pattern names.

suggestion.title: Malicious Model Version Registered in Vertex AI Registry from Hijacked Bucket
suggestion.rationale: Post-hijacking: attacker-supplied model reaches production registry. Pipeline should detect unauthorized model deploys or version-metadata tampering, but generated no impact-phase detection.
log_sources: Vertex AI Model Registry audit logs
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on models.create or models.update operations where source bucket is not in organizational whitelist, or model checksum diverges from CI/CD artifacts for same version label. Correlate: if model deployed to endpoint <1h after creation by non-standard principal, escalate as poisoning attempt.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Vertex AI Project Buckets and Naming Schemes
suggestion.rationale: Bucket squatting requires attacker to identify project naming patterns; pipeline missed detection of reconnaissance queries (LIST buckets, describe projects) preceding attacker bucket creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ListBuckets or ListProjects API calls from non-approved service accounts followed within 2h by CreateBucket operations with similar naming schemes. Flag if caller has no prior Vertex AI interaction history.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Standard asset-exposure hunt — the canonical Splunk SPL and Defender KQL live once in [...] Substitute this CVE wherever the template references <CVE>'. Pipeline generated zero use cases despite this direct instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-20253 against Splunk Enterprise asset inventory. Identify instances reachable from untrusted networks on default ports (8089, 8000). Flag any exposed instances pending patch application past due-date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability: 'missing authentication for critical function' via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Article specifies unauthenticated exploitation route; pipeline surfaced no detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints (typically port 9997–9999) lacking valid authentication tokens or X-Splunk-Input-Token headers. Alert on POST/PUT payloads to file-operation endpoints from external sources.

suggestion.title: File Creation/Truncation via Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker capability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. This file-manipulation vector is absent from pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file creation or truncation events in $SPLUNK_HOME initiated by unauthenticated sidecar connections. Alert on modifications to critical database or configuration files outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Log Truncation and Audit Trail Destruction
suggestion.rationale: Ability to 'truncate arbitrary files' enables erasure of audit logs, a defense-evasion tactic. Pipeline missed this secondary impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on truncation or deletion of transaction logs, audit logs, or database WAL files in Splunk infrastructure. Flag any such operations correlated with prior unauthenticated sidecar endpoint access.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No auth required; any network-exposed sidecar port is an attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to /_sidecar/ or /_postgres/ paths (or sidecar enumeration patterns) originating from external IPs without valid Splunk session tokens. Flag 200/201 responses. Correlate source IPs against shodan/censys for Splunk instance inventories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious File Write/Truncate Operations from Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—file manipulation at scale is both data destruction (T1565.001) and potential persistence. Should hunt for anomalous file ops by Splunk processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid file creation/truncation attributed to splunkd or sidecar processes outside expected working directories. Flag bulk deletes to log paths. Correlate with unauthorized sidecar endpoint hits from same timeframe.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV = active exploitation. Pipeline must generate CVE-specific IDS rule. Article establishes attack pattern: missing auth + file ops.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Splunk HTTP requests lacking authentication tokens + subsequent file-write syscalls from Splunk process. IDS rule: flag POST/GET to sidecar endpoints from sources not in trusted CIDR. Federal patch due 2026-06-21 defines urgency window.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Instance Inventory Against CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'public-facing application'—must scan for exposed Splunk versions. Vulnerability requires network exposure to be exploitable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query scanner output for Splunk Enterprise instances unpatched for CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference asset management DB to identify instances with external-facing ports (8000, 8089). Prioritize instances exposed to internet. Flag any updated after 2026-06-21 as potential post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Port Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as attack vector. Reconnaissance scanning for this service should be a hunt target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network scanning activity (SYN sweeps, service enumeration) against Splunk infrastructure. Flag repeated connection attempts to sidecar ports (often 5432-derivative, or custom ports). Correlate with external source IPs attempting HTTP enumeration.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the attack vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the critical access pattern is absent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated network connections to the Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint from untrusted networks. Track successful connections without credential exchange. Correlate with subsequent file system modifications on the Splunk host.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: The payload is explicit: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this behavioral indicator is completely missing from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, deletion, or truncation operations on the Splunk Enterprise host sourced from or proxied through the PostgreSQL sidecar process. Prioritize unexpected operations to sensitive Splunk directories and system paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerability Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends baseline vulnerability scanning against this CVE; the basic inventory detection is absent. Federal remediation deadline is 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index all Splunk Enterprise instances across the fleet. Flag any with product version matching CVE-2026-20253's affected range as critical priority. Cross-reference with external network exposure data to prioritize remediation of internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause is 'missing authentication for critical function'—detection must focus on endpoint exposure and lack of access controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound network traffic to the PostgreSQL sidecar service port from external or untrusted subnets. Alert on any attempts from non-Splunk administrative networks. Correlate with firewall rule changes that may have widened access scope.

suggestion.title: Fake Software Update Download & Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Fake Update Lures'—core ClickFix infection vector. No detection rule generated despite this being the initial access point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for executables matching Windows/software update naming patterns (.exe, .msi, .scr) downloaded from non-Microsoft CDNs and executed from temp/Downloads. Correlate download source reputation and file signature validation failures.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Loader Execution from User Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'new loaders' as malware delivery mechanism; execution phase detection missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or recently-signed executables spawned from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Downloads, or %UserProfile% with secondary network I/O or suspicious child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe).

suggestion.title: Staged Malware Fetch Post-Loader
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'expand malware delivery' implies multi-stage: loader fetches secondary payload. Command-and-control phase entirely absent from kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections (HTTP/HTTPS to non-whitelisted destinations, DNS to unregistered domains) from loader processes within seconds of user-initiated execution, especially with .exe parent in user directories.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Threat Actor IOC Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article name-checks ClickFix campaign; should correlate to known malware family signatures, registry keys, C2 domains. No actor/campaign identified in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate process/file artifacts (names, registry keys, strings) against published ClickFix tooling signatures. Detect obfuscation techniques (XOR, API hashing, string encoding) documented in ClickFix variants.

suggestion.title: Browser-Spawned Child Process With Unsigned Binary Execution
suggestion.rationale: Social engineering delivery model (user clicks link/download from browser). Detection for browser→exe→network chain not present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes with ancestry explorer.exe or browser process → unsigned .exe in user directories → immediate outbound connection. Raise alert on first-seen unsigned binary execution chains within 30 seconds of download.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Management Port
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user' can exploit; MITRE T1190 implies network exposure. Core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound TCP connections to Splunk management ports (8089, 8000) lacking valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Alert if POST/GET requests to /services/data/* or /admin/* endpoints return success without Authorization header.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack vector: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'. Requires monitoring for unauthorized access to internal service endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor access to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically localhost:5432 or named pipe access). Alert on SQL commands (CREATE TABLE, DROP, TRUNCATE) executed via sidecar without authenticated Splunk process context.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'create or truncate arbitrary files'; this is the direct impact and should be detected at filesystem level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation operations by splunkd or sidecar processes in unexpected directories (outside standard Splunk/var/lib/splunk paths). Flag TRUNCATE operations on config files, encrypted indices, or audit logs.

suggestion.title: Scanning for Exposed Splunk Instances
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV context implies reconnaissance phase; article references 'exposed assets'. Network scanning for Splunk should precede exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple failed connection attempts to port 8089/8000 across internal or DMZ ranges, or successful connections followed by HTTP OPTIONS/HEAD probes to /_status endpoint without authentication.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Detection via Patch Status
suggestion.rationale: Article cites CVE-2026-20253 as the canonical identifier; standard asset inventory and patch tracking required for CISA KEV compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise versions prior to patched release. Cross-reference against vulnerability scanner results. Flag systems where splunkd process version matches vulnerable range (obtain from Splunk advisory) but patch not applied by federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Langflow BaseFileComponent tar extraction with parent-directory traversal symlinks
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'symlink-traversal' as the core vulnerability mechanism but existing UC_2_2 only hunts for POST to upload endpoints, not the actual tar extraction or symlink creation. Article states vulnerability is in 'BaseFileComponent-based nodes' unpacking TAR, implying local extraction with symlink following.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow processes executing tar, untar, or Python tarfile operations on uploads directory; correlate with creation of symlinks to sensitive paths (/etc, /.ssh, /.aws) in tmp or Langflow working directories within seconds of tar extraction. Flag if symlink target count exceeds 5 per extraction.

suggestion.title: JWT authentication bypass via forged bearer tokens in Langflow API calls
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1606.001 (Forge Web Credentials: Web Cookies) but UC_2_4 title mentions 'post-JWT-forge' with no actual hunt for JWT tampering. Attack requires forging valid-appearing JWT to bypass authentication; need detection for malformed, unsigned, or expired JWT tokens in Authorization headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt HTTP requests to Langflow API endpoints with Authorization: Bearer headers where JWT signature verification fails, claims are missing (exp, iss, aud), or token was created with a non-standard key. Flag any Authorization header modification within 10 seconds of a 401 response followed by a 200 response.

suggestion.title: Python Interpreter node code execution with dynamic imports and system commands
suggestion.rationale: Article title and UC_2_4 imply 'Python Interpreter node' is the RCE endpoint, but detections focus on child-process spawning, not the actual arbitrary Python code execution within Langflow. Need detection for eval/exec/compile/import statements with untrusted input.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow worker processes for Python bytecode execution (compile, exec, eval, __import__) where arguments originate from HTTP request parameters. Correlate HTTP POST to endpoints containing 'python', 'interpreter', 'eval' with child-process creation within 100ms.

suggestion.title: File and directory enumeration via repeated 404/403 responses from Langflow file endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1083 (File and Directory Discovery) but no hunt. Exploitation requires discovering target file paths before symlink traversal; attacker likely probes with ../ patterns or /etc/passwd guesses, generating 404 responses.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP clients that send >10 requests to Langflow /api/v1/files or /api/v2/files endpoints within 60 seconds with distinct file paths, especially if requests contain ../ sequences or absolute paths (/etc, /.ssh) in parameters.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized component registration or dynamic import of Langflow modules
suggestion.rationale: Article lists T1525 (Implant Internal Image) suggesting attacker implants or modifies Langflow components post-exploitation. Need detection for unexpected component loading, module imports from non-standard paths, or modifications to component registries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow component directories (/langflow/components, /app/langflow/components) for file modifications or creation outside of package manager operations. Correlate with Python import statements targeting these directories or non-standard sys.path entries in Langflow process environment.

suggestion.title: Langflow CVE-2026-55255 — POST to /api/v1/responses (IDOR endpoint surface)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines UC_3_1 in 'Recommended hunts' section with Splunk SPL and Defender KQL. Pipeline extracted zero use cases. Article phrase: 'POST to /api/v1/responses (IDOR endpoint surface)'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to /api/v1/responses endpoint from authenticated users. Baseline by user, source IP, and destination to identify cross-user flow execution attempts indicating IDOR exploitation.

suggestion.title: Langflow IDOR enumeration — single source fan-out POSTing to /api/v1/responses
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines UC_3_2 with aggregation logic: >20 requests in 5m window. Article phrase: 'single source fan-out POSTing to /api/v1/responses' indicates systematic enumeration. Pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect a single authenticated user or source IP generating >20 POST requests to /api/v1/responses within 5-minute windows, indicating automated enumeration of victim flow IDs.

suggestion.title: Asset exposure — Langflow CVE-2026-55255 vulnerability match
suggestion.rationale: Article references UC_3_3 under 'IOC-driven hunts': 'Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)' with recon phase, high confidence. Template-referenced but pipeline should have called it out.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory and vulnerability scanners for instances running Langflow versions affected by CVE-2026-55255. Correlate with successful authentication to prioritize exposed systems.

suggestion.title: Crossplane ImageConfig signature verification disabled or modified
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Crossplane allows package signature verification to be configured via the `ImageConfig` mechanism.' An attacker could disable this defense entirely. No detection for ImageConfig tampering or disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to ImageConfig CRDs that disable cosign verification or set verification policy to permissive/none. Flag any changes to ImageConfig.spec.packagePullPolicy or ImageConfig.spec.skipSignatureVerification fields.

suggestion.title: OCI registry image manifest change between verification and pull
suggestion.rationale: Article describes TOCTOU: 'malicious OCI registry could serve a correctly signed image for verification... [then different content for installation].' This is the core attack—verifier checks Image A, installer pulls Image B. No detection for this divergence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate cosign verification success events with actual image pull events. Flag cases where image digest at verification time differs from digest at pull time, or where manifest layers differ between check and use phases.

suggestion.title: Cosign signature verification success followed by unsigned package installation
suggestion.rationale: The TOCTOU window: signature verification passes but content installed lacks valid signature or doesn't match verified content. Article notes packages are 'correctly signed for verification' then 'unverified package content' installed—a content mismatch.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Crossplane package installations where cosign verify exit code is 0 (success) but the installed package checksum or signature state does not match the verified artifact. Compare package metadata pre- and post-installation.

suggestion.title: Rapid mutable-tag re-tagging during Crossplane package installation
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must re-tag image quickly between verification and pull phases. No detection for suspicious tagging activity correlated with package installation timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect OCI registry tag operations (re-tag, overwrite) on mutable tag references occurring within seconds of corresponding cosign verify or image pull operations by the same Crossplane instance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Gravity SMTP System Report Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'requests to `/wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data` found in web server access logs, particularly those including the `?page=gravitysmtp-settings` query parameter' as the explicit exploitation signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP GET requests to `/wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data` with query parameter `page=gravitysmtp-settings` from sources lacking valid WordPress admin session cookies. Alert on 200 responses; correlate against Wordfence-published source IPs if available.

suggestion.title: WordPress System Configuration Enumeration via Plugin REST API
suggestion.rationale: Article states endpoint returns 'comprehensive JSON "System Report" generated by the plugin' containing 'WordPress configuration details, including installed plugins, themes, and software versions' and 'Database configuration details, including server version and table names.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response bodies for JSON payloads containing plugin/theme inventory, database table enumeration, or PHP version strings returned from gravitysmtp REST endpoints. Alert on unauthenticated access returning detailed system metadata.

suggestion.title: Credentials Exfiltration – API Keys and OAuth Tokens via Gravity SMTP
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists exposed credential types: 'API keys, secrets, and OAuth tokens for configured email integrations' and 'Credentials for third-party email services, including Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, and Zoho.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP responses from `/wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data` containing credential patterns (oauth_token, api_key, secret, aws_access_key). Flag JSON responses mentioning SES, Mailjet, Resend, Zoho, or Google in credential context.

suggestion.title: Mass Scanning for CVE-2026-4020 – Gravitysmtp Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article reports: 'exploitation activity spiked on June 7, with 4 million requests being blocked that day' and 'Wordfence firewall has blocked more than 17 million attempts.' This indicates widespread reconnaissance/scanning campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline HTTP requests to `/wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data`. Alert on threshold exceedance (>50 requests/minute across infrastructure, or >5 requests/minute from single source IP). Correlate with 404 responses (non-existent endpoint) to identify scanning distinct from legitimate use.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Version Detection – Vulnerable Versions ≤2.1.4
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'affects all versions of the plugin from 2.1.4 and older and has been addressed in version 2.1.5, released on March 17.' Requires identifying vulnerable plugin versions in system enumeration data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: When System Report data is captured in logs/WAF, extract Gravity SMTP version string. Flag installations reporting version ≤2.1.4 as vulnerable to CVE-2026-4020. Correlate with patch deployment tracking to identify unpatched instances.

suggestion.title: GentleKiller Framework Execution or Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'GentleKiller EDR Framework.' Pipeline extracted zero IOCs or tool signatures. Expected detection: process creation, file writes, or registry artifacts matching tool name or known command-line patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation, file writes, or registry modifications containing 'GentleKiller' string or known variant hashes. Track execution from temporary, system, or AppData directories. Correlate with EDR/security product process termination attempts.

suggestion.title: Mass Security Process Termination Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article states targeting '400 Security Processes.' This is a defense-evasion hallmark. Pipeline recognized no kill-chain phase for this attack pattern despite explicit mention in title.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process termination or suspension of known EDR/security tools (Defender, CrowdStrike, Sophos, etc.) via taskkill, wmic, Get-Process | Stop-Process, or registry unload. Flag attempts to target >5 security processes in rapid succession. Establish baseline of expected security-process names for false-positive tuning.

suggestion.title: RaaS Infrastructure Command & Control Beacon
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'The Gentlemen RaaS'—a ransomware-as-a-service operation. RaaS infrastructure implies C2 communication, operator consoles, and payload staging. Pipeline returned no kill-chain or C2 detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS POST requests with suspicious User-Agent strings, excessive retry patterns, or beaconing intervals. Correlate with lateral movement, process termination, and file encryption events. Flag communications to known RaaS C2 infrastructure or newly registered domains associated with Gentlemen operators.

suggestion.title: EDR Evasion via Anti-Tamper or Hook Injection
suggestion.rationale: GentleKiller explicitly framed as 'EDR Framework.' This suggests active defense-evasion tactics such as driver-level hooks, AMSI bypass, or ETW manipulation. Pipeline identified no privilege-escalation or defense-evasion techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet (driver loading), suspicious .sys/.dll writes to System32 or drivers directory, and kernel-mode process creation. Detect AMSI bypass attempts (registry disables, DLL hijacking of amsi.dll). Flag unsigned drivers or recently modified security callback hooks.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payload Staging and Encryption Activity
suggestion.rationale: RaaS operations stage payloads before execution. Article implies ransomware delivery (title: 'The Gentlemen RaaS'). Pipeline generated zero detection use cases for impact or collection phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for high-volume file modifications with new extensions (.gentlemen, .ransom variants), batch file execution for encryption orchestration, and WMI commands targeting remote hosts. Correlate file encryption artifacts with previous process termination events and EDR disabling attempts.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-EDR Disabling
suggestion.rationale: Once security processes are disabled, attackers pivot. Article does not detail this, but it is standard RaaS playbook. Pipeline surfaced no lateral-movement techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After EDR process termination events, detect SMB enumeration (net view, net share), PSEXEC execution, WinRM lateral movement, or Kerberoasting attempts. Flag RDP/SMB traffic to multiple internal hosts from previously-clean systems within minutes of successful EDR disabling.

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE HTTP Exploitation Request Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'actively exploited Joomla JCE Flaw'—no use case was generated for detecting exploitation attempts to JCE endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP POST/GET requests to /components/com_jce/ or similar JCE paths containing encoded payloads, suspicious parameter injection, or null-byte sequences. Establish baseline for legitimate JCE admin traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Server Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'PHP Code Execution' as exploit outcome; pipeline missed execution-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP interpreter (php, php-cgi, php.exe) spawned as child of web server process (httpd, Apache, nginx, IIS) with suspicious arguments (-r, -d, eval) or inline code execution. Correlate timing with prior HTTP requests to JCE endpoints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Creation in Web Directories
suggestion.rationale: RCE via JCE typically results in webshell persistence; pipeline missed persistence-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php, .phtml, .phar files created in web-accessible directories (htdocs, www, /var/www) with timestamps immediately following JCE HTTP requests or PHP execution events. Flag file paths containing obfuscation or random naming.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or C2 Callback from Compromised Web Server
suggestion.rationale: CISA active-exploitation warning implies post-compromise attacker command execution and exfiltration; standard for RCE workflows but not surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PHP process execution with outbound DNS or TCP connections to non-whitelisted external IP/domain. Look for immediate timing correlation (within seconds) and unusual port selection (non-80/443).

suggestion.title: Splunk API Requests Lacking Authentication Headers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user' can exploit via service endpoint. Need to hunt for requests to Splunk critical functions missing Authorization or session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk HTTP access logs for GET/POST requests to /api/v2/*, /admin/*, /services/* endpoints that lack Authorization header, X-Auth-Token, or valid session cookie, yet return 200/201. Alert on unauthenticated writes to sensitive endpoints (users, app_configs, file_manager). Baseline legitimate internal IPs and flag external-origin matches.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthorized Connection Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as attack vector. Hunt for unexpected connections or command execution against internal database service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar logs for connection attempts from IPs outside expected Splunk service whitelist. Alert on SQL commands attempting file operations (COPY, pg_read_file, pg_write_file) or spawning shell subprocesses. Detect TCP connections to sidecar port (typically 8191 or custom) from unauthenticated clients.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation in Splunk Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'. Impact detection for unauthorized filesystem writes to Splunk config/data paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for FileCreate/FileWrite events in $SPLUNK_HOME/etc, /opt/splunk/var, and configuration directories from unexpected processes (nginx, python sidecars). Alert on truncation of .conf, .db, audit.log, or monitoring data files. Correlate timing with unauthenticated API requests to PostgreSQL sidecar in preceding seconds.

suggestion.title: Asset Inventory: Splunk Instances Vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: KEV indicates active exploitation. Need sweep to identify exposed Splunk instances with missing authentication enforcement on critical functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run authenticated and unauthenticated probes against Splunk API endpoints (curl -k https://<ip>:8089/services/server/info without auth) across all assets. Flag instances returning 200 without credentials or auth bypass. Cross-reference against patch-management system for CVE-2026-20253 hotfix deployment. Escalate any unpatched instances reachable from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration Integrity Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'truncate arbitrary files'—adversary may disable auth controls via config modification. Monitor for suspicious auth/access configuration changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor audit.log for modifications to auth.conf, inputs.conf, limits.conf, props.conf via API PUT/POST. Alert on direct filesystem writes to $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/ that bypass API logging. Flag deletion or size reduction of audit.log itself. Check for unexpected role/capability additions granting 'admin' or 'can_delete_all_objects' to default/system accounts.

suggestion.title: Splunk Sidecar Process Execution Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: PostgreSQL sidecar exploitation could spawn unexpected child processes. Monitor for shell or command-injection artifacts from sidecar context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ProcessCreationEvents where parent = postgresql sidecar and child is /bin/sh, /bin/bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or file-manipulation binaries (cp, rm, tee, dd). Alert on unexpected child spawning from sidecar. Correlate process creation events with prior unauthenticated API requests within 30-second window.

Correlate with sidecar process events and unauthenticated network access logs to confirm the attack chain.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanning – Patch Compliance Gate
suggestion.rationale: Federal due date (2026-06-21) and CISA KEV status require scanner coverage and patch status confirmation across all Splunk Enterprise instances as compliance baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ensure all Splunk Enterprise instances have been scanned for CVE-2026-20253 vulnerability status within the last 7 days. Generate and retain audit report documenting instance FQDN, product version, patch status, and remediation date. Flag any unpatched instances and escalate to remediation team with federal deadline context.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the endpoint itself is the exploitable surface and should be actively monitored for unexpected access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically port 5432 or custom) from external/untrusted sources. Look for connection attempts that lack valid Splunk authentication headers or originate from non-internal subnets. Baseline normal internal traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is the direct impact and should be detected through file system operations initiated via the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PostgreSQL sidecar network access (from UC1) with unexpected file creation or truncation events on the Splunk server filesystem. Flag any file operations on security-sensitive paths (config, certs, plugins) preceded by unauthenticated sidecar connection within seconds.

suggestion.title: Data Destruction via CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: File truncation capability described in article represents potential data destruction impact; detections should focus on tampering indicators post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncation operations (SetEndOfFile, truncate syscalls) on critical Splunk data directories without corresponding administrative activity logs. Combine with evidence of unauthorized PostgreSQL sidecar access to confirm exploitation vs. routine operations.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Version Inventory
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation in the wild; federal due-date is 2026-06-21. Asset exposure hunt baseline required before detecting exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate all Splunk Enterprise instances on the network (via process name, listening ports, banner grabbing) and cross-reference against known-vulnerable version range. Flag any unpatched instances still exposing sidecar endpoints to networks outside trusted administrative subnets.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM auth bypass: Host header value present in 401-then-200 sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A crafted Host could therefore make the auth gate evaluate a different route from the one FastAPI dispatches.' UC_102_3 detects the sequence but doesn't correlate on the Host header value itself. Attackers craft a specific Host value to bypass auth—tracking that same value across the 401 and 200 responses would confirm the injection was the exploit vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify requests to /key/*, /user/*, etc. that receive 401 on first request (with Host header X), then 200 on second request with identical Host header X from same source. The persistence of the crafted Host value across both requests proves the bypass was Host-driven, not a legitimate re-auth.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM HTTP request: uri_path and Host-derived-path mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The auth layer derived the effective route from request.url.path... Starlette reconstructs from the Host header... make the auth gate evaluate a different route.' Direct detection of the vulnerability's root cause: parse Host header, extract implied path, compare to actual URI path. Mismatch = attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For requests to admin endpoints, extract path from the Host header (if present) and the actual request URI. If Host-derived path differs from URI path (e.g., Host: api.example.com/../admin vs URI: /key/list), flag as potential exploit. This directly mirrors the vulnerability mechanics.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM: successful admin write (POST/PUT/DELETE) to /key, /user, /team endpoints without Bearer or API-key auth
suggestion.rationale: Article management routes (/key/*, /user/*, /team/*, etc.) should never accept write operations unauthenticated. The vulnerability allows bypass of auth checks on these endpoints. This is a higher-specificity hunt than UC_102_5 (which accepts GET too).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST, PUT, or DELETE requests to /key/*, /user/*, /team/*, /model/*, /customer/*, /spend/*, /organization/* endpoints that return 200/201/204 and lack Authorization or X-API-Key headers. Write operations to these endpoints without auth are a hard exploit signal.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM source accessing multiple admin categories post-probing (temporal correlation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes reconnaissance probes (/health, /version, /docs) followed by exploitation. Combined UC_102_6 (probes on ports 4000/8000/8001) + UC_102_4 (enumeration). A source that probes /health, /version, /docs *then* attempts to access /key/*, /user/*, /team/* within 10 minutes is a scripted attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate reconnaissance requests (/health, /version, /docs) with subsequent admin-endpoint enumeration from the same source within a 10-minute window. Temporal clustering of probe → enumerate → exploit is a strong attack signature.

suggestion.title: LiteLLM rapid state-changing admin endpoint access (key creation, user deletion, configuration change) in short window
suggestion.rationale: Once auth is bypassed, attacker enumerates then makes state changes (creates API keys, deletes users, modifies spend limits, etc.). Article endpoints are all admin-facing, suggesting config/user management. Post-exploitation activity is rapid.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequences of POST/PUT to /key/create, /user/delete, /spend/modify, /model/add endpoints from a single source within 5 minutes, especially if they result in 201/200 and previously had failed auth attempts from the same source.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerable Splunk Enterprise Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CVE: CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' CISA KEV context indicates active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability management platform for systems running Splunk Enterprise versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Prioritize externally exposed instances. Correlate with network exposure scans to identify remotely accessible targets.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability vector: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports from external or untrusted networks without corresponding Splunk authentication events. Alert on successful connection establishment followed by file-system access.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct impact phase exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk service account for unexpected file creation or truncation in $SPLUNK_HOME, /etc, or /var directories. Correlate with preceding network anomalies on sidecar ports. Baseline normal Splunk deployment activity to reduce false positives.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Splunk Management Ports
suggestion.rationale: T1190 exploitation requires exposed application. Article states 'exploit public-facing application' and CISA KEV indicates active abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan perimeter for Splunk web (8000), Splunk daemon (8089), sidecar, and PostgreSQL ports reachable from internet. Cross-reference open instances with patch inventory. Recommend firewall rule hardening or WAF placement.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Configuration File Modification Post-Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: File truncation/creation could target Splunk auth or persistence configs. Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to $SPLUNK_HOME/etc (inputs.conf, props.conf, limits.conf, auth config) immediately following unauthenticated sidecar activity. Use file-integrity monitoring or syslog audit logs. Alert on unexpected ownership or permission changes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the initial attack surface—external network access to a protected service without auth credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 or documented custom) from external sources without prior auth session. Monitor for TCP connection attempts to these ports on Splunk hosts; establish baseline of legitimate internal traffic and flag anomalous external access.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation Without Authentication Context
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability explicitly allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files.' File operations are the exploitation payload and must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events on Splunk systems where the initiating process is PostgreSQL or unauthenticated sidecar service. Build whitelist of expected Splunk file operations and flag unexpected file creation in config, var, or bin directories.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Public Port Exposure
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV designation confirms active wild exploitation. Attack requires 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' reachable from internet. Port exposure must be detected and inventoried.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query external port-scanning data (Shodan, Censys) and internal port-scan results for Splunk instances exposing PostgreSQL service ports to untrusted networks. Cross-reference findings against internal asset inventory and alert on unexpected exposure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status and Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20253 is explicitly named and CISA-required for remediation by 2026-06-21. Vulnerability scanner integration for this CVE is mandatory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ensure vulnerability scanners detect CVE-2026-20253 across all Splunk Enterprise instances. Alert on any system returning vulnerable status. Correlate with patch management to identify unpatched systems and reconcile against Federal remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass Followed by File System Modification
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain pivots on 'missing authentication for critical function' enabling file operations. Correlation of auth-failure or missing-auth with subsequent file creation/truncation is the behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate missing authentication events (failed auth logs or unauthenticated endpoint access logs) with file creation/truncation events on the same Splunk host within 60 seconds. Alert on this sequence as strong indicator of CVE-2026-20253 exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct description of exploitation vector with zero authentication enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints (typically internal-facing) from external sources or without authentication headers. Baseline expected requesters (legitimate Splunk management) and alert on deviations with status codes indicating success (200, 201).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — file-system operations are the exploitation outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag file create or delete operations initiated by Splunk sidecar/PostgreSQL processes with destinations outside normal Splunk directories (config, var/log, var/run). Truncate operations on critical files (authentication DBs, logs) are highest fidelity.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status = actively exploited in wild; unauthenticated exploitation requires internet-facing Splunk endpoint. Core detection gap: identify vulnerable assets before they're exploited.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and internet-facing asset databases for Splunk Enterprise instances (port 8089 mgmt, 8000 web UI). Cross-reference against patched versions post CVE-2026-20253 fix; prioritize any unpatched instances for immediate remediation due to federal deadline (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: Splunk Authentication Bypass via Missing Auth Control
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability described as 'missing authentication for critical function' — the core technical flaw is absent or bypassable auth on a sensitive endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect successful (HTTP 200/201) requests to /services/sidecar or PostgreSQL endpoints that should require authentication (check for missing auth headers, invalid tokens, or requests from unauthenticated sources). Spike in auth bypass attempts or sudden successful unauthenticated requests is high-fidelity.

suggestion.title: Cross-realm alarm access by authenticated user — IDOR boundary violation detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An authenticated user in any realm can delete alarms belonging to other realms.' This is the defining exploitation step. Current UCs do not detect a user accessing resources outside their assigned realm; this gap allows the core attack to pass undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract tenant/realm ID from URL path (/api/{realm}/alarm). Correlate with user's home realm from auth logs or identity provider. Alert when user issues DELETE to a realm not assigned to their account. Baseline known cross-realm admin accounts and alert on first-time or unusual patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk alarm deletion anomaly by non-admin user — impact pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'bulk delete' as the attack vector. Only administrators should bulk-delete alarms. A non-admin user deleting 20+ alarms signals either account compromise or successful IDOR exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline DELETE volume by user role. Alert when a non-admin user issues ≥20 DELETE requests to /api/*/alarm within 10 minutes, or when their delete rate exceeds historical median by 5x. Cross-reference with failed authorization events (401/403) in preceding 10 minutes to distinguish opportunistic IDOR from account-compromise abuse.

suggestion.title: Authorization failure cascade preceding successful cross-realm deletions — boundary-probe pattern
suggestion.rationale: IDOR exploitation often follows a probe-and-exploit sequence: attacker triggers authorization failures (401/403) on restricted realms, then succeeds on exploitable ones. If logs capture per-request auth decisions, this pattern indicates boundary testing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In a 5-minute window, flag sequences where a user receives ≥2 auth failures (401/403 status) on DELETE /api/{realm}/alarm, immediately followed by ≥3 successes (200/204) to the same or different realm. Indicates attacker systematically testing which realms they can access.

suggestion.title: Rapid sequential alarm-ID guessing across realms — enumeration with realm-switching
suggestion.rationale: UC_1_1 detects generic enumeration. Article implies attacker supplies 'arbitrary' alarm IDs—likely sequential guessing. If attacker alternates realms while guessing IDs, they amplify coverage while spreading requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DELETE /api/{realm}/alarm requests where the URL alarm ID parameter increments sequentially (1, 2, 3... or detected via regex/delta analysis) AND the realm path alternates (realm1, realm2, realm1...). This indicates systematic enumeration across multiple tenants, distinguishing from single-realm probing.

suggestion.title: Langflow IDOR: Successful unauthorized flow access (HTTP 200 + cross-ownership)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'execute any flow belonging to another user.' UC_3_1 detects any POST to endpoint; this detects successful *unauthorized* access via HTTP 200 where user_id ≠ flow_owner_id. Exploitation signal, not just presence on endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log HTTP 200 responses to /api/v1/responses where authenticated user_id does not own the flow_id in request. Join Langflow flow-ownership table (user:flow mapping) against request logs. Single or repeated cross-ownership access indicates IDOR breach.

suggestion.title: Langflow: Flow execution by non-owner
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'execute any flow.' Access without execution is incomplete. Need hunt for Langflow execution logs showing a flow run by user_id who did not create/own it. Kill chain missing the final impact step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Langflow execution audit logs. Alert when flow run event shows executor_id ≠ flow_owner_id. Spike in cross-ownership execution or rapid sequential runs by single user on flows they don't own = post-breach activity.

suggestion.title: Langflow IDOR: Learning-phase enumeration (403→200 cascade)
suggestion.rationale: Real-world IDOR exploitation shows trial-and-error: 403 on wrong flow_id guesses, then 200 on correct guess. Article doesn't mention this behavior, but it's a forensic indicator absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect source_id with multiple 403 errors to /api/v1/responses in 10-minute window followed by 200 success. Ratio of 403:200 > 3:1 within same time window = enumeration learning curve.

suggestion.title: Langflow: Exfiltration-sized responses from /api/v1/responses
suggestion.rationale: IDOR + large response body = data exfiltration. Article mentions accessing another user's flows; response-size anomaly hunt absent. No baseline comparison for /api/v1/responses response-size envelope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline typical response size for /api/v1/responses (e.g., median 3–5 KB). Alert on responses >10× baseline or > 1 MB, especially from /api/v1/responses outside business hours or from rare source IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Gravity SMTP REST API Endpoint Probing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies `/wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data` as the attack vector. Wordfence states 'key indicator of compromise is requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data found in web server access logs, particularly those including the ?page=gravitysmtp-settings query parameter.' Exploitation spiked to 4 million blocked requests on June 7, 2026.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unauthenticated HTTP GET requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data returning HTTP 200. Requests containing ?page=gravitysmtp-settings query parameter are high-confidence exploitation indicators. Establish per-site baseline for this endpoint; trigger on 10x+ volume increase within 1-hour window or any requests from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP System Report Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the REST endpoint response returns comprehensive JSON containing 'API keys, secrets, and OAuth tokens for configured email integrations' and 'Credentials for third-party email services, including Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, and Zoho.' This is structured credential disclosure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP 200 responses from /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data for JSON payloads containing credential-bearing fields. Use regex patterns to detect api_key, oauth_token, access_token, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, zoho_token, mailjet_key, resend_api_key. Flag responses >10KB returned to non-authenticated clients.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin and PHP Version Enumeration via Gravity SMTP
suggestion.rationale: Article lists exposed report contents including 'installed plugins, themes, and software versions,' 'Server and PHP environment information,' and 'database configuration details, including server version and table names.' This is post-compromise reconnaissance for attack planning.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP 200 responses from Gravity SMTP endpoints containing JSON with structured arrays/objects listing plugins, themes, or key-value pairs for php_version, mysql_version, wordpress_version, installed_plugins, or database_tables. Correlate with concurrent vulnerability scanner user-agents (wpscan, nikto) or mass-scanning IP blocks.

suggestion.title: Mass Scanning for Vulnerable Gravity SMTP Instances
suggestion.rationale: Article reports Wordfence 'blocked more than 17 million attempts' and 'exploitation activity spiked on June 7, with 4 million requests being blocked that day. Similar activity was recorded for several days afterward.' High-volume anomaly is a critical early-warning signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline volume of requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data per Gravity SMTP-using WordPress site. Alert on 100x+ spike in 15-minute window from 10+ distinct source IPs. Geolocate source IPs; cross-reference against known mass-scanning infrastructure and public indicators shared by Wordfence.

suggestion.title: Abuse of Exfiltrated Email Service Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'The exposure of live third-party API credentials means an attacker could abuse the site's connected email services' and stolen credentials enable attackers to 'impersonate the victim to third parties.' Compromised Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, Zoho accounts enable spam/phishing campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for abnormal API authentication or SMTP transactions to email service providers (AWS SES SendEmail calls, Google Workspace APIs, Mailjet endpoints) from IP ranges associated with compromised WordPress installations. Alert on bulk email sending patterns from previously dormant service accounts starting June 7, 2026.

suggestion.title: Batch Termination of Security Processes (400+ targets)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'targeting 400 Security Processes' — this is the core attack vector. Pipeline missed generating detection for abnormal bulk termination of EDR, AV, and security tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes terminating multiple security/EDR/AV processes in short time window. Look for taskkill, Get-Process | Stop-Process, or direct API calls targeting defender, edr, antivirus process names in batch (>5 in 60s).

suggestion.title: GentleKiller EDR Framework Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'GentleKiller EDR Framework' — this is a named malware tool that should be IOC-tracked and detected on execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution, DLL loading, or registry writes matching 'GentleKiller', 'gentle*killer', or similar variants. Monitor for unsigned/untrusted code loading in kernel drivers or system processes.

suggestion.title: EDR Tool Modification or Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Framework targets 400 security processes — implies modification/deletion of EDR binaries, config, or drivers. Article phrase 'GentleKiller EDR Framework' indicates attack specifically targeting EDR agents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion/modification of EDR/AV/security tool directories, binaries, or service registry keys. Monitor for writes to ProgramFiles/EDR vendors, HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services (security-related), or /etc/security/ paths.

suggestion.title: Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) Execution Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'The Gentlemen RaaS' — the RaaS distinction indicates command-and-control orchestration and staged deployment. Pipeline did not surface RaaS kill-chain indicators (staging, callback, ransom demand).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect C2 beacons to Gentlemen RaaS infrastructure. Monitor for encrypted or obfuscated outbound connections from compromised hosts with suspicious TLS/DNS patterns. Correlate with process-kill signatures to identify multi-stage execution.

suggestion.title: Registry/Service Disablement of Security Tools
suggestion.rationale: EDR targeting framework would disable services; RaaS attacks commonly disable services before encryption. Pipeline missed service-level evasion despite 'targeting 400 security processes' implying systematic disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services with Start value set to 4 (disabled) for security-related services. Monitor for sc.exe, powershell Stop-Service, or wmic service calls targeting Defender, EDR, or AV services.

suggestion.title: Kernel Driver Loading for EDR Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Named framework 'GentleKiller EDR Framework' suggests kernel-level capability. EDR-targeting tools commonly use vulnerable or malicious drivers to bypass user-mode protections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or vulnerable driver loading following process-termination spikes. Monitor DeviceImageLoadEvents for DLLs/drivers with suspicious hashing, lack of valid signatures, or loading from temp/user-writable paths in correlation with high process-termination events.

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE Component Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes actively exploited flaw in JCE (Joomla Content Editor) allowing PHP execution — core attack vector should be detectable via HTTP request patterns to /plugins/editors/jce/ paths with suspicious parameters or file upload attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to /administrator/ or /plugins/editors/jce/ endpoints with suspicious parameters (file upload, code injection markers). Look for requests lacking proper Joomla session tokens or from unauthenticated sources attempting to access JCE administrative functions.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via JCE Upload
suggestion.rationale: JCE is a file manager plugin that allows content uploads — malicious actors will abuse upload functionality to place PHP shells. Article establishes execution vector is PHP code; detect file operations in JCE directories followed by code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious file writes to /plugins/editors/jce/media/ or related JCE directories (look for .php, .phtml, .php5 extensions) with immediate child process spawning from web server (php.exe, apache2, nginx) with suspicious command-line arguments or network connections.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Installation in JCE Directories
suggestion.rationale: Successful exploitation of Joomla JCE will result in attacker uploading web shells to writable JCE folders. Article warns of active exploitation suggesting shells are being deployed — detect anomalous PHP files in editor upload paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation of new .php files in /plugins/editors/jce/media/ and sibling directories with entropy/size anomalies compared to legitimate plugin files. Monitor for subsequent HTTP requests to newly created PHP files (180+ second correlation window).

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE Manager Authentication Bypass Indicators
suggestion.rationale: If JCE flaw involves authentication bypass or privilege escalation, detect access to JCE administrative functions without valid authentication tokens or from low-privilege sessions attempting privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla access logs for requests to /administrator/index.php?option=com_jce or /plugins/editors/jce/admin requests originating from unauthenticated or guest user accounts, or session-hopping behavior (single source IP chaining multiple User-Agent patterns and session IDs).

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell Callback from Compromised Joomla
suggestion.rationale: PHP RCE via JCE typically leads to reverse shell callback to attacker infrastructure. Article establishes code execution is possible; detect outbound network connections from web server to unusual destinations with shell protocols.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP connections from web server processes (apache, php-fpm, IIS) to non-whitelist external IPs on ports 4444, 5555, 8080, 9001 or DNS queries to suspicious domains from web server context, especially within seconds of JCE upload/execution events.

suggestion.title: Joomla Database Modification Post-JCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often modify Joomla database to create backdoor admin accounts or alter permissions after exploiting JCE. Detect database writes to users/sessions tables from unexpected contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected write operations to Joomla database files (jos_users, jos_user_sessions) or SQL queries altering user privileges/password hashes executed from PHP child processes spawned outside normal request-response lifecycle.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user...through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — requires detection for exposed service endpoints and unauthorized access attempts to Splunk admin interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise admin endpoints (/admin, /services/admin, /splunkd) and direct connection attempts to PostgreSQL sidecar service port. Flag requests without valid authentication tokens or API keys originating from external/untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — requires detection of file operations initiated by database service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL command logs and Splunk filesystem events for unexpected file creation/truncation operations (e.g., COPY TO/FROM commands, table truncation on system tables). Correlate with unauthenticated API calls to sidecar endpoint. Alert on data loss in Splunk indexes.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must discover the exposed PostgreSQL sidecar port before exploitation — article indicates service is network-accessible and requires prior reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect port scanning patterns targeting PostgreSQL default port (5432) or Splunk sidecar variants against Splunk Enterprise instances. Flag service version enumeration probes. Alert on external scanning of multiple management ports on single Splunk host.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unpatched Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status and federal due date 2026-06-21 mandate urgent patching; article states CVE 'observed exploited in the wild' — requires asset inventory hunt for vulnerable versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances with version < [patched_version]. Cross-reference network segmentation logs for instances where PostgreSQL sidecar port (or Splunk management ports) is accessible from untrusted networks or public internet.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: 'unauthenticated user' accessing critical function. Pipeline missed the exploitation mechanic itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In Splunk audit logs, detect HTTP 200/201 responses on admin or REST endpoints (e.g., /services/server/config, /services/data/*, PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints) where the request lacks a valid auth token or originates from an untrusted source. Baseline: all such endpoints require auth headers or internal service whitelist.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Operations via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline omitted the post-exploitation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk hosts for file creation/truncation by postgres or sidecar processes targeting system-critical paths (config dirs, binaries, data stores) without corresponding administrative change tickets. Anomalous deletions of log files or config backups indicate data destruction or anti-forensics.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Exposure Hunting (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Requires exposed instance; article: 'unauthenticated user' implies internet-facing or network-accessible. Pipeline missed foundational asset-exposure hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances on non-standard ports or public-facing via shodan/censys queries for 'splunk' or 'splunkd'. Correlate with firewall rules and NAT policies. Flag unpatched Splunk instances against known-affected versions. Federal SOCs: track patching against CISA KEV due date (2026-06-21).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Enumeration and Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly mentions 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the abuse point. Pipeline failed to isolate this service as a detection surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthenticated connections to PostgreSQL sidecar ports (default 5432 or Splunk-specific sidecar ports) from external or untrusted internal subnets. Monitor for unusual queries or file-system operations originating from the sidecar process. Alert on port scanners probing these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the initial attack surface and must be detectable via missing/invalid authentication on requests to Splunk internal endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically internal port 8089 or configured alternates) originating from external/untrusted sources and lacking valid authentication tokens or session cookies. Correlate by destination process (splunkd, postgres sidecar) and external source IP patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write via Splunk Service Process
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — this requires detection of suspicious file creation/deletion operations performed by Splunk service processes outside normal configuration directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, deletion, or truncation events where source process is Splunk Enterprise (splunkd.exe, postgres backend, sidecar service) and target path is outside /opt/splunk/etc or %SPLUNK_HOME%\etc. Prioritize alerts on system-critical paths: Windows\System32, Program Files, service binaries, scheduled tasks, temporary directories with persistence indicators.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Pattern — Unauthenticated Sidecar POST Requests
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20253 is the explicit vulnerability; detection must trigger on requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints without authentication, correlated with active KEV status indicating in-the-wild exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST/PUT requests to known Splunk sidecar endpoint paths that lack Authorization headers or contain invalid/expired tokens, originating from non-administrative sources. Include payloads with path traversal characters or OS-command patterns. Cross-check vulnerability scanner results; patch verification is mandatory within 11-day federal window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Escalated File Operations on System Binaries
suggestion.rationale: File truncation via unauthenticated access could enable follow-on persistence if leveraged to modify executables or configurations that Splunk runs with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate file truncation or deletion events from Splunk processes with subsequent file write operations to the same path within 10 seconds. Flag if target files are Windows executables, service binaries, scheduled task files, or scripts — not under Splunk configuration scope.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the core attack vector and must be detected; the missing-auth vulnerability is the explicit attack surface.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation on Splunk Enterprise Hosts

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation operations originating from Splunk service processes (splunkd, PostgreSQL sidecars) where the operation lacks corresponding legitimate config/management triggers. Focus on files in unexpected directories (system binaries, application roots, startup locations).
