suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated connection attempts to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar (port 5432 or custom). Flag successful connections from external/unexpected sources lacking corresponding auth logs. Query splunkd.log for connection_status=failed entries; absence combined with subsequent file operations is suspicious.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized File Creation or Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the destructive payload execution; pipeline missed it entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for open()/truncate() syscalls with O_TRUNC flag on Splunk hosts. Alert on file size drops to zero in $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/*/default/ or var/lib/ outside deployment windows. Correlate with sidecar endpoint access logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active exploitation in the wild and federal patch deadline 2026-06-21. Article recommends standard asset-exposure hunt per template; pipeline produced zero guidance despite this being the canonical CISA KEV hunt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-20253 exposure across all Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference patch dates against 2026-06-21 deadline. Splunk-native: search for license_master version below patched threshold; check Splunk Cloud API for SaaS instance versions.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure via Network Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires discoverable PostgreSQL endpoint. Article describes external access; missing reconnaissance phase covering port enumeration and service exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar port (5432 or custom) from non-admin sources or external networks. Monitor failed authentication attempts to port 5432 in splunkd.log. Correlate with subsequent file operations.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Integrity Changes to Splunk Config Files
suggestion.rationale: Article says 'truncate arbitrary files' — if attacker truncates inputs.conf, limits.conf, or app configs, this is persistence/defense evasion. Missing post-exploitation config-tampering detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline file hashes for $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/*/default/inputs.conf, limits.conf, props.conf. Alert on unexpected modifications outside maintenance windows. Flag any file with size reduction (truncation indicator) on critical Splunk binaries or configs.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scan Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists CVE-2026-20253 as CISA KEV with federal remediation deadline and active exploitation. Recommended hunts section references vulnerability scanning as primary detection method, yet pipeline generated zero scanning use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Splunk Enterprise instances are flagged as vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253 by authenticated or network vulnerability scanners. Cross-correlate detection timestamp with patch-management records to identify unpatched instances still at risk.

suggestion.title: Internet-Exposed Splunk Enterprise Management Port
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) as threat vector, implying Splunk instances must be externally accessible for exploitation. Pipeline generated no network-exposure detection despite this being prerequisite to attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Splunk Enterprise management port (8089) and web console (8000) reachable from untrusted networks. Alert on externally-accessible instances without firewall/VPN gating, especially if patch status for CVE-2026-20253 is unverified.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Connection Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack surface: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline generated zero detection for this precisely-defined access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST/GET requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar port (typically 5432 or proxied through management port 8089) from external IPs lacking valid authentication headers or credentials. Flag connection attempts that include file-manipulation parameters.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' Pipeline generated zero behavioral detection for the post-exploitation impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk server filesystems for unexpected file creation or truncation outside maintenance windows, correlated with unauthenticated sidecar access attempts or abnormal PostgreSQL process activity. Alert on modifications to Splunk config, app, or binary directories.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Process Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies PostgreSQL sidecar as attack surface enabling file operations. Pipeline generated no process-level behavioral detection despite this being the execution mechanism for the vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar process spawns unexpected child processes, makes external network connections, accesses files outside normal scope, or exhibits resource exhaustion. Correlate with network reconnaissance or CVE-2026-20253 scanning activity.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Compliance Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes federal patch due-date (2026-06-21) and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline generated zero compliance-tracking or deadline-enforcement use case despite regulatory emphasis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference Splunk Enterprise asset inventory against patch-management records. Flag any instance not updated to a patched version by federal due-date (2026-06-21) for immediate escalation to compliance and incident response teams.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the primary attack vector for initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs and network traffic for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (commonly ports 8089, 8191, or custom) from unauthenticated sources. Alert on POST/PUT requests to file-manipulation endpoints lacking valid authentication tokens or certificates.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status confirms active exploitation. Pipeline must detect scanning and exploitation activity targeting Splunk Enterprise vulnerability endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect reconnaissance and exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2026-20253 in Splunk Enterprise. Monitor for version enumeration, scanning of vulnerable sidecar endpoints, and unauthenticated requests to file-manipulation services. Baseline activity and alert on spikes or mass scanning patterns.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—operational success indicator if exploitation is achieved.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation or truncation operations from Splunk service accounts or sidecar processes. Baseline normal file I/O patterns; flag deviations in critical directories (/etc, /opt/splunk/etc, database paths, authentication config) or suspicious file timestamps/sizes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV with federal patch due-date 2026-06-21. Standard asset-inventory hunt for unpatched Splunk Enterprise; article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanners and asset inventories for Splunk Enterprise versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with patch-management logs to identify patch lag. Prioritize externally-exposed instances and compare against federal due-date timeline.

suggestion.title: Authentication File Tampering via File Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'truncate arbitrary files' capability directly enables tampering with auth config. Truncation of auth.conf or PostgreSQL connection files bypasses authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for truncation or size reduction of Splunk authentication and credential files (auth.conf, passwords.conf, postgresql.conf, connection strings). Alert on unexpected file modifications in /opt/splunk/etc or PostgreSQL config directories; flag any auth-file changes coinciding with unauthenticated sidecar access patterns.

suggestion.title: HTTP inline-remote request to rclone RC endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector: article states 'rclone rcd --rc-serve accepts unauthenticated GET and HEAD requests to paths of the form /[remote:path]/object. The remote value is parsed from the URL and passed to normal backend initialization.' Direct initial-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rclone RC port (5572) for GET/HEAD requests with bracketed inline-remote syntax: /[, %5B (encoded), :path=, config_is_local. Correlate with unexpected command execution child processes.

suggestion.title: Rclone RCD spawning shell or command-execution child process
suggestion.rationale: Article attack mechanism: 'Inline remote configuration can set backend options that execute local commands during initialization.' RCE execution phase detection with high fidelity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rclone/rclone.exe parent spawning cmd.exe, powershell, bash, sh, or network utilities (curl, wget, nc, ncat, socat). Requires baseline of legitimate child processes if any exist.

suggestion.title: Rclone RCD launched without authentication mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Article: vulnerability requires 'unauthenticated' access. Precondition: rclone rcd --rc-serve launched without --rc-user, --rc-pass, --rc-htpasswd, --rc-key, or --rc-cert flags.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rclone process with 'rcd' or '--rc-serve' that lacks all authentication flags. Separate alert for public-interface binds (0.0.0.0, ::, :any-port).

suggestion.title: Software inventory: vulnerable rclone versions 1.46–1.74.2
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-49980 affects rclone 1.46 through 1.74.2 (fixed in 1.74.3+). Inventory scan identifies at-risk assets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for rclone where Major=1 and Minor in [46..74] excluding (Minor==74 and Patch>=3). Cross with processes running --rc-serve or systems with port 5572 listening.

suggestion.title: Browser process connection to localhost rclone RC port (CSRF/SSRF)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Drive-by Compromise' technique (T1189). If user browses malicious site while rclone rcd runs locally, JavaScript can exploit via CSRF to localhost:5572.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, Brave processes establishing connections to 127.0.0.1:5572 or [::1]:5572. Correlate timing with malicious site visit or unpatched rclone inventory.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names CVE-2026-20253 as the exploited vulnerability with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-21. No detection use case generated to identify vulnerable Splunk Enterprise instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on vulnerability scanner detection of CVE-2026-20253 in Splunk Enterprise. Cross-reference patch deployment logs; flag all unpatched or unmitigated instances and escalate any not remediated by the federal due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—the specific attack vector. No detection for exploitation of this endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints for unauthenticated or anomalous requests. Detect successful file creation, truncation, or write operations without prior authentication. Alert on any access from unexpected network sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Truncation on Splunk Enterprise Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes the impact as 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—the direct exploitation outcome. No filesystem-level detection for this activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise servers for unexpected file creation, truncation, or modification in critical directories (etc, bin, var/lib, config). Correlate filesystem events with PostgreSQL sidecar service activity and PostgreSQL process execution. Flag operations outside normal administrative baseline.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Service Port Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack surface. No network-based detection for anomalous or external access to this internal service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports for unusual source IPs, geographic anomalies, or external/internet-origin traffic. Flag failed authentication attempts and connection patterns inconsistent with legitimate administrative access.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the attack vector; detect HTTP/network traffic to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports from external sources without Splunk authentication headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for inbound connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (typically ephemeral or hardcoded port alongside Splunk management services, port 9997 or 8089 range). Alert on unauthenticated POST/GET requests lacking valid Splunk authentication tokens. Cross-reference with asset inventory to identify exposed instances not behind VPN/firewall.

suggestion.title: File Truncation in Splunk Application Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—this is the impact mechanism; detect FileDelete or FileWrite events with truncation semantics in %SPLUNK_HOME% paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file-truncation or file-overwrite operations in critical Splunk directories (app configs, var/log, etc.) from Splunk service processes or unexpected user contexts. Alert on zero-byte or truncated files in Splunk state directories. Correlate with network logs showing prior unauthenticated access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Exploitation Attempt (PostgreSQL Sidecar File Abuse)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes specific attack pattern—unauthenticated file-write via PostgreSQL sidecar—map to known exploit signatures or request patterns specific to this CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint containing file-operation payloads (e.g., parameters indicative of path traversal, file-write commands, or truncate operations). Correlate with vulnerability scanner results showing CVE-2026-20253 exposure. Alert on any match regardless of HTTP response code (adversary may not trigger visible error).

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Service Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article presupposes 'public-facing' Splunk services exploited by multiple threat actors (CISA KEV), requiring prior discovery; detect network reconnaissance for Splunk management ports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for port-scan or service-enumeration patterns against known Splunk ports (8089, 9997, 8000) originating from external networks. Alert on banner-grab attempts or repeated connection attempts across multiple ports in short time windows. Correlate with known Splunk version-detection probes.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration File Integrity Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: File truncation would corrupt Splunk's internal state; monitor for configuration inconsistency alerts or failed Splunk service startup post-compromise, indicating successful file manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk internal logs (_internal index, splunkd.log) for file-read errors, configuration parse failures, or corrupted state indicators. Alert on unexpected Splunk process restarts or service degradation correlated in time with file-access anomalies or network exploitation attempts. Cross-check integrity hashes of critical Splunk config files if available.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Service Endpoint Access Outside Expected Maintenance Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'unauthenticated' access to internal endpoint—this violates normal Splunk administration patterns; detect off-hours or anomalous caller IPs accessing management interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate Splunk administration traffic (IP ranges, time windows, user accounts). Alert on access to Splunk management ports (8089) or internal service endpoints from external/unexpected IP space, after-hours, or with zero authentication attempts/failures preceding successful connection. Raises urgency if correlated with known Splunk CVE-2026-20253 exposure.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct exploitation requires detecting requests to normally-authenticated endpoints lacking credentials.

Baseline: legitimate Splunk clients always include auth tokens. Flag missing auth + successful 200 response.

suggestion.title: Splunk Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation by Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File system activity from sidecar service (typically splunk user) to unexpected paths signals exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file creation and truncation in /opt/splunk/var/lib/splunk, /opt/splunk/etc, and /var/log triggered by splunk service account outside normal maintenance windows. Baseline file operation patterns per Splunk deployment. Alert on file size collapse (truncation) in index or config directories.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Asset Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article: T1190 'Exploit Public-Facing Application' implies exposure. Vulnerability only exploitable against internet-accessible instances; requires passive discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Splunk Enterprise web UI accessible from non-internal networks. Cross-reference exposed instances against patch status for CVE-2026-20253. Flag unpatched + externally routable = critical until remediation by 2026-06-21 deadline.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'missing authentication for critical function' — anomalous requests bypassing auth layer. Monitor request patterns that should fail but succeed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on requests to /services/*/properties or sidecar management endpoints that return 200/201 without valid session tokens or Bearer headers. Sequence detection: repeated 401→successful access = potential bypass attempt.

suggestion.title: Splunk Index/Audit Log Truncation or Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Article: file truncation capability enables post-compromise evidence removal. Truncation of _internal or audit indexes erases attack telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk index file sizes and event counts. Alert on unexpected drops in /opt/splunk/var/lib/splunk/*/db/* size or _internal index event count baseline deviation. Correlate with file truncation events from splunk service account.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Changes to Splunk Auth Layer
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'missing authentication' may indicate config manipulation. Post-exploitation could involve disabling auth modules or modifying authentication enforcement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor changes to authentication-related Splunk configs (/opt/splunk/etc/auth*, /opt/splunk/etc/system/local/default.conf). Alert on modifications to nginx reverse proxy configs or PostgreSQL service startup flags that disable or bypass authentication checks.

suggestion.title: Asset inventory — Langflow version <1.9.1 vulnerable to CVE-2026-55255

suggestion.title: Langflow IDOR confirmed exploitation — flow execution by non-owner user
suggestion.rationale: Article UC_4_4 specified as actions-phase hunt (High confidence) detecting successful unauthorized execution. Pipeline generated zero use cases from article body.

suggestion.title: Langflow IDOR lateral abuse — spike in multi-owner flow execution

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on plugin version detection requests or responses containing Gravity SMTP version strings ≤2.1.4. Monitor plugin update events for sites missing patch from March 17 release.

suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific query parameter signature '?page=gravitysmtp-settings' used in exploitation. Should trigger on presence of unusual page parameters on /wp-json endpoints.

suggestion.title: Email Service Credential Compromise via Plugin Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states exposed credentials allow attacker to 'impersonate the victim to third parties' and abuse email services (Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, Zoho). Should detect abnormal email service API usage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email service APIs (SES, Gmail, Mailjet, Resend, Zoho) for authentication from unusual locations/IPs following exploitation window (post-June 7). Alert on bulk email sending, credential changes, or domain configuration modifications.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' The endpoint is the attack surface; detect requests without valid credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP(S) traffic to Splunk Enterprise instances for requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication headers (missing Authorization tokens, invalid session credentials, empty auth fields). Correlate with Splunk audit logs for failed authentication against the sidecar endpoint.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Creation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Monitor file operations originating from PostgreSQL process for anomalous paths and rapid succession.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events where the source process is PostgreSQL sidecar or child of sidecar, or where created/modified files deviate from expected Splunk directories (var/lib/splunk, $SPLUNK_HOME/etc). Flag rapid file truncation in succession and write access to OS-critical paths.

suggestion.title: Hunt for Exposed PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article describes unauthenticated exploitation, implying sidecar is network-accessible. Conduct asset-exposure hunt for Splunk Enterprise instances with sidecar listening on non-loopback interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Network scan for listening PostgreSQL sidecar ports on Splunk Enterprise hosts (typically variant of port 5432 or custom endpoint). suggestion.rationale: Article states 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct impact of successful exploitation, distinct from initial access and must be monitored separately.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated sidecar access with subsequent file creation/deletion events. Flag TRUNCATE and CREATE operations originating from or mediated through PostgreSQL sidecar service accounts, especially targeting Splunk directories.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure and Patch Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV status implies active exploitation; article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and sets Federal patch due date — asset-exposure hunt is canonical for CISA KEV entries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scans and asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-20253 patch status; identify unpatched instances and missing patch data, prioritizing externally-exposed assets.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via a 'service endpoint' — attackers must discover or target the exposed sidecar before exploitation; reconnaissance precedes the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for scanning or probing of common PostgreSQL ports (5432) and Splunk sidecar URIs. Correlate failed connection attempts and port-scanning patterns with subsequent successful exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Internet Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' through exposed endpoint. T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application) is primary attack vector — canonical asset-exposure hunt must run immediately before federal due date.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate vulnerability scanner detections for CVE-2026-20253 against Splunk Enterprise instances with egress routes to internet. Alert on any confirmed external accessibility to ports 8089 (mgmt) or 8000 (web).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack surface: 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' exploited without authentication. Direct HTTP/HTTPS requests to this endpoint from untrusted sources indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk instances for HTTP/HTTPS requests to sidecar endpoints (port 5432 or service-specific) from external IPs with missing or invalid auth headers. Baseline internal access patterns and flag external sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write from Splunk Service
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' File-system write operations by splunkd to unexpected directories (outside /opt/splunk/var) indicate successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or modification initiated by splunkd or Splunk-owned processes to /etc, /root, /var/log, or web directories. Establish baseline of legitimate Splunk write paths and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Log Truncation / Evidence Destruction Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article capability: 'truncate arbitrary files' enables attacker to destroy audit logs. Unexplained log-flow discontinuities or sudden log-file size reductions correlate with post-exploitation cover-up.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for gaps in Splunk/application audit logs on CVE-2026-20253 affected instances. Alert when expected log entries stop flowing or log files shrink without corresponding deletion events. Correlate across syslog, Splunk audit logs, and OS audit trails.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Suspicious Child Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation file-write capability enables attacker to write malicious scripts or binaries. Unexpected child process spawns from splunkd (bash, curl, wget, etc.) indicate secondary payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by splunkd or related Splunk processes with high entropy command lines or unexpected binaries (/bin/bash, /usr/bin/curl, /usr/bin/wget). Baseline legitimate Splunk process spawning behavior.

suggestion.title: Splunk Configuration File Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Arbitrary file-write capability enables persistence or lateral movement via modified configs (app.conf, inputs.conf, outputs.conf). Unauthorized config changes bypass normal change-control workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor integrity of /opt/splunk/etc/ configuration files. Alert on modifications outside maintenance windows with mismatched source process (not splunkd admin utilities) or unusual hash/timestamp deltas.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthenticated Endpoint File Operations (CVE-2026-20253)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No detection UC generated despite explicit attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit/access logs for unauthenticated requests to service endpoints or PostgreSQL sidecar paths. Flag file-creation or file-deletion operations initiated without prior authentication session, especially in index/data directories.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'create or truncate arbitrary files' impact. No impact-phase detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file truncation/deletion operations in Splunk's index, data, or configuration directories when initiated from PostgreSQL sidecar context or unauthenticated source. Correlate with failed or unauthorized authentication attempts.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as exploitation path. No sidecar-specific reconnaissance or access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar service for: (1) connection attempts from non-localhost addresses, (2) unauthenticated session initiation, (3) file I/O operations outside normal Splunk process behavior.

suggestion.title: Splunk CVE-2026-20253 Exposure Hunt (CISA KEV)
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due-date 2026-06-21 requires immediate fleet inventory and patch status verification. No vulnerability scanner or exposure-hunting UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner for Splunk Enterprise instances with CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with network exposure scans (internet-facing ports 8089, 8000, 9997). Flag all unpatched instances as P0 remediation due 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'missing authentication for critical function vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated user.' Detection must distinguish legitimate sessions from exploitative unauthenticated endpoint hits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs for API calls to critical endpoints (/services/admin, /services/data) lacking valid session tokens or with null auth headers. Correlate spikes in 401/403 responses to subsequent file-modification events on the system.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact attack vector: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This concrete service is the exploit channel and requires targeted monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connections to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar (internal port 5432 or custom endpoint) originating from external networks or non-admin user contexts. Flag DDL/DML statements (CREATE, TRUNCATE, DROP) executed post-connection from unauthenticated sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation on Splunk Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stated outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the impact and directly observable via filesystem telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unexpected file creation, deletion, or truncation in Splunk directories ($SPLUNK_HOME, config, data, backup) by processes other than splunkd. Correlate with prior PostgreSQL endpoint access or failed authentication attempts within the same timeline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Confirmation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends: 'CVE-2026-20253 — match against your vulnerability scanner.' Confirms Splunk instances patched for this specific CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output for Splunk Enterprise instances reporting CVE-2026-20253 status. Prioritize remediation on externally-facing instances; even patched systems warrant one sweep given patch-lag risk noted in article.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—this is the primary attack vector and requires detection on direct API/endpoint calls lacking authentication headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise instances for unauthenticated HTTP POST/PUT/DELETE requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typically internal management ports). Track requests lacking valid session tokens or API keys that attempt file creation, truncation, or arbitrary I/O operations. Correlate with vulnerability scanner alerts for CVE-2026-20253.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—requires behavioral detection for file system activity originating from Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation, truncation, or deletion initiated by Splunk sidecar processes (e.g., postgres, postgresql, sidecar service user) with unusual paths (config directories, data stores). Baseline normal sidecar file operations and flag deviations; correlate with network telemetry showing unauthenticated inbound requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Presence
suggestion.rationale: Article is CISA KEV entry—'only adds CVEs that have been observed exploited in the wild'—basic scanning and patch verification required as SOC baseline detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Match CVE-2026-20253 against vulnerability scanner output and asset inventory for all Splunk Enterprise deployments. Flag any systems reporting unpatched or patch-lag status as of federal deadline 2026-06-21. Cross-check patched assertions against running service versions.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet-Facing Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'—requires discovery that Splunk instances are reachable externally, the prerequisite for T1190 exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Splunk Enterprise instances with ingress ACLs permitting unauthenticated external access to management/sidecar ports. Flag as high-risk if running vulnerable versions of CVE-2026-20253. Generate exception report for justification of public-facing Splunk.

suggestion.title: Host-header injection to management routes (CVE-2026-49468 exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'A crafted Host header could therefore make the auth gate evaluate a different route from the one FastAPI dispatches.' This is the exploit mechanism itself—core detection target.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to LiteLLM management endpoints (/key/*, /user/*, /team/*, /model/*, /sso/key/generate, etc.) where the Host header contains injection markers (;, .., %20, @, 0x, \\, ?) or otherwise deviates from expected reverse-proxy or application hostnames. Hypothesis: attacker crafts Host to bypass route-matching in auth layer.

suggestion.title: Auth-gate evasion: 401/403 → 200 on protected route within 5m
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated access to protected management routes.' Direct sequence indicating successful bypass: rejection, then acceptance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP 401/403 then 2xx on same management route from same source within 5-minute window. If subsequent request uses different Host header or other attribute, boost confidence to high.

suggestion.title: Post-breach multi-category mgmt enumeration (CVE-2026-49468 discovery)
suggestion.rationale: After bypass succeeds, attacker discovers what resources are available. Article lists distinct management categories: keys, users, teams, models, spend, SSO, ACL—attacker would enumerate across categories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid successful access (2xx) to management endpoints spanning 3+ distinct categories (/key/*, /user/*, /team/*, /model/*, /spend/*, /sso/*) from same source within 10m. Post-exploitation reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated mgmt-route success: 2xx without auth headers
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated access to protected management routes.' Direct outcome: management endpoint replies 2xx to a request lacking any authentication credential.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 2xx status for protected routes (/key/generate, /user/new, /model/new, /sso/key/generate, /add/allowed_ip) where request contains no Authorization header, no x-litellm-api-key header, and api_key not in query string. High-confidence exploitation success.

suggestion.title: Recon of exposed LiteLLM via /health, /version, /docs from external source
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must discover the service. Article lists these as recon targets. Phrase: 'External recon of exposed LiteLLM proxy.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor non-RFC1918 sources querying multiple LiteLLM recon endpoints (/health, /version, /docs, /openapi.json, /redoc, /routes) in rapid succession. Threshold: 3+ distinct paths or 25+ hits in 1h. Indicator of active service discovery.

suggestion.title: Credential harvesting via /key/list or /user/list post-bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article lists /key/list and /user/list as protected management routes. After bypass, attackers would enumerate and exfiltrate credential material. Logical post-exploitation step not explicitly detailed in hunts above.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 2xx responses to /key/list, /user/list, /team/list, /customer/list from unauthenticated requests, especially when correlated with prior Host-header anomalies or auth-bypass signatures. Indicates credential enumeration and exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Splunk Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user' to access PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint. Pipeline generated no UC to detect such requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk web interface logs for HTTP requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (typical paths: /api/pgsql, /services/pgsql, or similar) originating from unauthenticated sessions or missing Authorization headers. Alert on POST/PUT/DELETE operations that bypass standard auth checks.

suggestion.title: Splunk Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar.' No use case addresses detection of file manipulation via the endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected file-system modifications (create, truncate, delete) on Splunk hosts with HTTP request logs showing sidecar-endpoint access. Look for writes to sensitive config, data, or log directories originating from PostgreSQL worker processes triggered by unauthenticated API calls.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Status & Exposure Scan
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies federal patch due 2026-06-21 and notes CISA KEV means active exploitation. Standard asset-exposure hunt is mentioned but pipeline generated no use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan all Splunk Enterprise instances for version matching vulnerable range (if known); cross-check against patch date. Alert on any instances still unpatched post 2026-06-21. Combine with network exposure scans to identify internet-facing Splunk web consoles.

suggestion.title: Splunk sidecar Endpoint Discovery & Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Attackers will need to discover and probe the PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint path. No reconnaissance-phase detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web logs for patterns of repeated 404 or 403 responses to potential sidecar paths (/pgsql*, /postgres*, /sidecar, etc.) followed by successful 200/201 responses. Spike in non-standard endpoint requests to Splunk from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin' as the attack surface and describes a bug being exploited. Title states 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug.' No use case generated despite being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Gravity SMTP plugin endpoints with known CVE parameters, POST requests to admin-ajax.php with Gravity SMTP action parameters, or 404/403 patterns indicating plugin enumeration prior to exploitation.

suggestion.title: API Key Extraction via Gravity SMTP Misconfiguration
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly identifies 'Expose API Keys' as the direct impact. No credential-access or exfiltration use case was generated despite this being the attacker's goal and objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to WordPress wp-config.php, plugin configuration files, or database tables containing SMTP credentials. Alert on bulk reads of wp-options or serialized credential objects from Gravity SMTP plugin directories.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SMTP Service Abuse Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Exposed API keys enable attackers to abuse SMTP service. Article describes 'hackers exploit' (compromise achieved) leading to key exposure, implying follow-on SMTP abuse is the impact driver. No collection/exfiltration use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMTP authentication with exposed plugin API keys, bulk email sends from WordPress server using exfiltrated credentials, or SMTP relay configuration changes tied to Gravity SMTP plugin compromise.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Directory Write Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Gravity SMTP plugin vulnerability may allow unauthenticated file write or code execution in plugin directory. Title describes exploiting a 'bug' in a plugin. No execution-phase detection generated despite plugin code-injection being typical attack progression.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious file creation or modification under /wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/ from web server process (www-data, IUSR). Alert on PHP file uploads or .htaccess modifications within plugin directory tied to HTTP requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious wp-admin Access via Compromised SMTP Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Exposed SMTP API keys may be associated with admin accounts or provide lateral movement to WordPress admin panel. No privilege escalation or lateral movement detection generated despite credential exposure typically enabling both.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate exposed API key usage in SMTP logs with concurrent wp-admin login attempts or access to /wp-admin/options.php (settings modification). Flag logins from IPs tied to SMTP abuse.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Configuration Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim: API keys exposed. Pipeline must detect when attacker reads plugin config. No data discovery or exfiltration use case generated despite 'expose' being the explicit attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database queries selecting from wp_options where option_name contains 'gravity' or 'smtp', or bulk file reads of /wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/settings.json. Detect credential data in outbound DNS, HTTP POST, or email events.

suggestion.title: Single user DELETE spanning unauthorized realms (IDOR confirmation)
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'An authenticated user in ANY realm can delete alarms belonging to OTHER realms.' Pipeline detects realm-switching but should explicitly correlate: did user succeed in deleting from a realm they don't own? Missing the core IDOR signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify users who issue successful DELETE requests (200/204) to alarm endpoints in realms where they have no assigned role or access grant. Cross-reference DELETE request realm against user's authorized realm list from identity/RBAC logs. Rapid deletions across 3+ non-owned realms in <5min window suggest IDOR exploitation.

suggestion.title: Alarm endpoint 400/422 errors preceding successful cross-realm DELETE
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may probe alarm IDs (malformed queries, invalid IDs) before discovering valid ones to delete. Article mentions 'supplying arbitrary alarm IDs' but no UC covers malformed request pattern before success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track sequences where a user issues 3+ requests to DELETE /api/*/alarm with HTTP 400/422 (bad request, validation error), then 1+ DELETE with 200/204 on different realm in same session. Pattern suggests ID enumeration across realm boundaries.

suggestion.title: OpenRemote DELETE request with user-controlled realm parameter tampering
suggestion.rationale: IDOR exploited by 'supplying arbitrary alarm IDs' — but also implicitly by tampering with realm in URL path. No UC explicitly covers detecting modified/anomalous realm values in DELETE requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DELETE requests where the realm in the URL path does not match the authenticated user's default/assigned realm and has no prior history with that user. Combine with 200/204 success response to indicate unauthorized cross-realm access.

suggestion.title: BaseFileComponent tar archive extraction with symlink path traversal
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'BaseFileComponent-based nodes arbitrary file read' and mentions 'tar extraction creates symlinks to sensitive paths'. UC_4_2 exists but is overly broad (any /etc/ file creation by Python). Should specifically detect symlink escape in archive unpacking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for symlink creation (not just file creation) during tar/archive extraction by Python-based Langflow processes. Symlinks should resolve outside their parent directory (e.g., /tmp/unpack/../../etc/passwd symlinks). Alert on symlink-to-sensitive-path creation within 5 seconds of tar invocation.

suggestion.title: Secret key material exfiltration post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: UC_4_3 discusses 'secret_key theft' enabling JWT forgery, but no UC captures the actual theft of the key material itself. Article states the exploit leads to 'arbitrary file read' which would include Django/Flask secret keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect read operations on Langflow secret key files (settings.py, .env files, config directories) by Python interpreter processes after BaseFileComponent exploitation attempts. Correlate with subsequent JWT signing operations within 1 hour.

suggestion.title: Docling/Unstructured/Video component initialization with malicious payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'Docling (DoclingInlineComponent)', 'Docling Serve (DoclingRemoteComponent)', 'NVIDIA Retriever (NvidiaIngestComponent)', 'Video File (VideoFileComponent)', and 'Unstructured API (UnstructuredComponent)' as vulnerable, but pipeline produces no component-specific UCs. No detection for malicious DOCX/video/API payloads triggering BaseFileComponent vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow component initialization (DoclingInlineComponent.run, UnstructuredComponent.run, VideoFileComponent.run) with file paths containing path traversal sequences (../, %2e%2e, etc). Correlate with subsequent Python subprocess spawning or file access to /etc, /.ssh, /.aws.

suggestion.title: T1081 credential harvesting from Langflow config/settings
suggestion.rationale: Article describes secret_key and JWT token theft but T1081 (Credentials in Files) is not mapped in MITRE techniques list despite being central to the attack—the exploit reads credentials from Langflow's settings/configuration files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file read operations on Django/Langflow configuration files (settings.py, .env, config.json, secrets.json) by non-administrative processes or from unexpected calling contexts (e.g., from web-accessible paths).

suggestion.title: Python eval/exec gadget chains in Langflow Python Interpreter node
suggestion.rationale: UC_4_4 captures subprocess spawning but misses inline code execution (eval/exec). Article mentions 'T1059.006 — Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python' as technique, implying Python eval chains. The 'Python Interpreter node RCE' likely chains through eval not just subprocess.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow Python Interpreter node execution for eval(), exec(), compile() calls with unsanitized input from previous nodes. Look for base64-encoded payloads passed to eval or dynamic code generation patterns.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS actionResourceJs response with JavaScript payload injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Arbitrary JavaScript Injection' but no UC detects whether the response actually contains injected script payloads. 'Arbitrary JavaScript Injection via Host Header Poisoning' is the core attack, yet detection focus is only on the request side.
log_sources: Web proxy logs with response body inspection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Craft CMS `/actions/app/resource-js` responses contain injected JavaScript (script tags, dynamic var assignments with attacker domain, Guzzle client initialization to non-org domain). Look for HTTP response bodies from this endpoint containing script-injection patterns or base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: SSRF exfiltration: outbound connection within 10s of resource-js request to same attacker domain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'forcing the application's... to fetched from attacker-hosted servers' but UC_6_2 only finds outbound connections generically. No detection correlates the poisoned request with the actual SSRF fetch. This closes the c2 visibility gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify requests to `/actions/app/resource-js` with suspicious Host headers, then correlate within 10 seconds with outbound HTTP/HTTPS from the web application to non-org destinations. Match source IP or web process. High fidelity if the attacker domain matches a known C2 sink.

suggestion.title: Admin privilege escalation via session-riding after resource-js exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Session-Riding RCE chain end' but no UC detects privilege escalation or session abuse. UC_6_3 finds plugin install but not the *privilege abuse* aspect. Need to detect admin actions (install, config change, user creation) from low-privilege contexts that correlate with prior resource-js requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Admin plugin-install or config-change POST requests from source IP that (a) previously accessed `/actions/app/resource-js` and (b) is not in the admin IP allowlist or does not match historical admin access patterns. Indicates session hijacking or privilege abuse.

suggestion.title: Craft CMS instance discovery and vulnerability enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article does not mention pre-exploitation reconnaissance, but attackers typically scan for Craft CMS instances before attempting exploitation. Should detect `/actions/app/resource-js` requests with HEAD/GET/OPTIONS probing from external IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inbound HTTP requests to `/actions/app/resource-js` with HEAD, OPTIONS, or GET from external IP ranges (non-org) without corresponding admin sessions. Bulk scanning patterns (multiple endpoints hit from same src IP in <1 min) raise confidence.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP REST API Reconnaissance Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data?page=gravitysmtp-settings as the indicator of compromise. 17M+ blocked attempts and June 7 spike prove active mass exploitation. This is the attack vector; pipeline extracted zero IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web server access logs for GET requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data with query parameter page=gravitysmtp-settings. Alert on spikes (>100 requests/min or >3σ deviation from baseline). Endpoint returns System Report JSON containing API keys, OAuth tokens, DB config, and installed plugin inventory—sensitive even if endpoint access is denied.

suggestion.title: Email Service Credential Exfiltration via Gravity SMTP Leak
suggestion.rationale: Article states disclosed credentials 'for Amazon SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, and Zoho' allow attackers to 'abuse the site's connected email services' and 'impersonate the victim to third parties.' Pipeline missed credential-usage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate email service API logs (SES, Google Workspace, Mailjet, Resend, Zoho) for anomalous access using exposed credentials: unusual originating IPs, geographies, API call patterns, or bulk email-send operations. If Gravity SMTP API key leaked, flag any API calls 24–72 hours post-compromise.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin & Theme Enumeration via REST API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies endpoint returns 'WordPress configuration details, including installed plugins, themes, and software versions.' This reconnaissance data 'significantly lowers the effort required to plan further attacks.' Pipeline missed enumeration detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated unauthenticated requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/* or /wp-json/wp/v2/plugins endpoints from same source. Correlate with requests to known-vulnerable plugin endpoints (e.g., /wp-json/breeze-cache/) if library versions in plugin list match historical CVE fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Sensitive Data Exfiltration via Misconfigured REST Permission Callback
suggestion.rationale: Article root-causes the flaw to 'permission_callback' always returning 'true,' exposing 'API keys, secrets, and OAuth tokens' and 'Database configuration details, including server version and table names' without authentication. Pipeline missed permission-bypass detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 200 responses from /wp-json/* endpoints that contain secret/token/password_reset fields to unauthenticated requests (no Authorization header or expired session). Inspect response bodies for patterns: 'secret', 'api_key', 'oauth_token', 'db_version', 'table_' to detect information disclosure.

suggestion.title: Volumetric Exploitation Spike Detection for CVE-2026-4020
suggestion.rationale: Article reports concrete timeline: exploitation spike June 7 (4M requests blocked in one day), sustained activity thereafter. Wordfence tracked daily metrics. Pipeline missed volumetric detection tied to this CVE's known exploitation window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create rolling 24-hour baseline for requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data. Alert if requests exceed baseline by >200% or spike >500 requests/hour. Correlate request sources across datacenter IP ranges and residential proxy services; June 7–30, 2026 exploitation window suggests automated mass scanning.

suggestion.title: Database Reconnaissance via Gravity SMTP System Report Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article specifically mentions 'Database configuration details, including server version and table names' returned by REST endpoint. This is OSINT-level reconnaissance enabling SQL injection or direct database attacks. Pipeline missed database-leakage detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for responses from /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data containing database version strings (e.g., 'MariaDB 10.5.15', 'MySQL 5.7.32'), WordPress table names (wp_posts, wp_users, wp_options), or connection strings. Flag if endpoint access precedes failed database authentication attempts or SQL injection probes.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — requires detection of unauthorized endpoint access that should require authentication
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint paths (inspect Splunk config for exact URI patterns) when no authenticated session exists or from unexpected source IPs. Baseline internal-only traffic; flag any external origin hits.

suggestion.title: File Creation or Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article attack outcome: 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — requires detection of file operations directly attributed to sidecar process or triggered by sidecar-endpoint access
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PostgreSQL sidecar process file-write operations with requests to vulnerable endpoint. Flag truncations of config, binary, or data files. Alert on file creation in unexpected paths (e.g., /etc, user homes, temp with persistence patterns).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure – Splunk Enterprise Patch Lag
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with federal due-date 2026-06-21 — article implies all Splunk Enterprise versions vulnerable until patched; standard asset-exposure hunt mandatory
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference scan results for CVE-2026-20253. Flag instances with patch missing or applied after 2026-06-21. Verify all exposed instances (internet-facing, DMZ) for baseline connectivity to PostgreSQL sidecar ports from untrusted networks.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PostgreSQL Sidecar Port Access Patterns

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Requests to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoints
