suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk inbound logs for HTTP requests to sidecar endpoints (commonly 127.0.0.1:8191 or internal service ports) lacking valid session tokens, X-Splunk-Authorization headers, or authentication cookies. Flag POST/PUT/DELETE requests from external or untrusted sources to /services/* paths without auth context.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—requires file-system activity detection on Splunk hosts, particularly writes outside normal operational directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On Splunk Enterprise hosts, detect file operations (creation, truncation, deletion) initiated by sidecar/PostgreSQL processes (typically splunkd user) writing to unexpected directories (/etc, /usr/bin, /var/lib outside Splunk paths). Correlate with absence of corresponding legitimate administrative activity in Splunk audit logs.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Instances on Public-Facing Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer'; standard inventory cross-reference for vulnerable Splunk versions (CVE-2026-20253) with internet-routable access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query process logs for Splunk version strings (splunkd processes); cross-reference against known vulnerable version ranges for CVE-2026-20253. Correlate with network exposure data (ports 8000, 8089, 8191 visible to external scanners or WAF logs). Flag instances matching both criteria for immediate remediation.

suggestion.title: Anomalous PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Invocation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies exploitation through 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'; unexpected activation or unusual request patterns to internal service ports indicate exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for requests to internal sidecar endpoints in Splunk audit/access logs (normally admin-only, low-volume, authenticated). Alert on anomalous spikes, requests from previously-unseen external IPs, or requests with HTTP 2xx responses when auth should have been required.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Direct evidence of auth-bypass exploitation path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports for HTTP POST/GET requests lacking authentication headers or valid session tokens. Alert on any non-error response (200, 201, 204) to sidecar endpoints from untrusted networks. Establish baseline of legitimate sidecar callers (internal Splunk processes) and flag external sources.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Truncation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers can 'truncate arbitrary files' via the sidecar endpoint. Impact-layer detection for confirmed exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file truncate operations (ftruncate, truncate syscalls) initiated by Splunk service processes or from network context of sidecar listeners. Flag truncations of critical files (configs, logs, binaries). Correlate with preceding sidecar access logs.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation via Splunk Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article states capability to 'create...arbitrary files' through sidecar. Complements truncation detection; identifies both write and destruction paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected file creation from Splunk service processes in non-standard directories (e.g., /root, /etc, /var). Combine with network context: file creation correlating to recent sidecar endpoint access from unauthenticated sources. Establish whitelist of expected Splunk file-creation locations.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Exposed Port Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'public-facing application' (KEV implies exposure). Asset-exposure hunt for sidecar listening on unexpected interfaces/networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Run periodic port scans and compare against baseline. Splunk sidecar typically runs on non-standard high ports (5432-adjacent or 9000+ range depending on config). Alert if sidecar port becomes reachable from internet-routable addresses or untrusted subnets. Cross-reference with inventory: which Splunk instances have patches for CVE-2026-20253?

suggestion.title: Splunk Authentication Bypass Indicator: Sidecar Calls Without Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing authentication'—core of this CVE. Detect calls to sidecar endpoints in absence of auth tokens, session IDs, or API keys.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse Splunk and sidecar service logs for API/endpoint calls with empty or missing Authorization headers. Baseline legitimate service-to-service calls (which may intentionally omit creds in internal networks). Flag external-origin requests missing credentials. Compare request pattern to known-good traffic from patchlevels ≥ [vendor fix version].

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Match + Exploit Attempt Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article classifies as CISA KEV: 'currently being exploited.' Combine vulnerability scanner hits with behavioral signals to confirm active exploitation vs. false alarm.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert with elevated severity when vulnerability scanner confirms Splunk Enterprise vulnerability to CVE-2026-20253 AND concurrent access logs show sidecar endpoint queries from suspicious IPs. Use threat intel for known exploit PoC traffic patterns. Correlate scanner date with access log timestamps to identify lag between exposure discovery and exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious POST Requests to Joomla JCE Component
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'actively exploited Joomla JCE flaw'—exploit delivery almost always occurs via HTTP POST to /index.php?option=com_jce or similar. Pipeline missed web-based initial-access detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests containing 'com_jce' or 'jce' in URI, especially with suspicious parameters, base64-encoded payloads, or PHP function names (eval, system, exec, passthru) in request body. Flag requests from non-administrative IPs to known JCE exploitation endpoints.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution via Unexpected eval() or system() Calls
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'PHP Code Execution' as impact. Without detection for in-process execution of dangerous PHP functions post-exploitation, impact is invisible. Pipeline generated zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes spawning child processes (bash, cmd, powershell) or executing system commands. Monitor PHP error logs for eval() attempts. Flag php.exe/php-fpm with unusual arguments or working directories outside expected application paths.

suggestion.title: File Upload or Write to Web-Accessible Directory During JCE Request
suggestion.rationale: Successful JCE exploitation typically results in webshell or file placement; article says 'actively exploited,' implying post-exploitation file artifacts. No use case for file-system write detection during web activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP requests to JCE endpoints with subsequent file creation/modification in /components/com_jce/, /tmp/, /var/www/html, or other web-root subdirectories. Flag PHP file writes with timestamps within seconds of malicious POST requests.

suggestion.title: Joomla Vulnerable Component Access Pattern (JCE Version / Feature Abuse)
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'JCE flaw'—should trigger detection for abnormal access patterns to known vulnerable endpoints or parameters. Pipeline did not surface component-level indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to Joomla administration or media management endpoints (/administrator/index.php, /media/, /images/) combined with JCE parameter manipulation (media=..., task=...). Detect requests with incomplete or malformed JCE parameters typical of CVE scanning/exploitation.

suggestion.title: High-Volume or Automated Exploitation Attempts Against Joomla
suggestion.rationale: CISA warning of 'actively exploited' flaw implies widespread scanning/attack activity. Pipeline should flag reconnaissance or mass-exploitation patterns even without specific CVE details.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate requests from single source IP targeting multiple /index.php?option=com_jce variants or common Joomla paths (/administrator, /components) in short timeframe (< 60s). Flag source IPs with > 5 JCE-related requests or error patterns (404→200→500 sequences).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Enterprise Vulnerable Instances
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry with active exploitation and federal due date 2026-06-21. Article identifies 'unauthenticated user' exploitation path. No asset-exposure hunt was generated despite being foundational for all downstream detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan enterprise for Splunk Enterprise instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-20253. Cross-reference with asset inventory and network boundary data to identify internet-exposed deployments. Flag any instance accessible from untrusted segments without authentication enforcement.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthenticated Access to Splunk Critical Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly specifies 'unauthenticated user' access to endpoints. No detection rule was generated for missing/bypassed authentication on Splunk admin functions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk admin endpoints (/admin, /etc, /services/configs) from untrusted sources that lack valid authentication tokens or return 200 without session validation. Monitor for unauthenticated POST/PUT attempts to critical paths.

suggestion.title: Detect PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Endpoint Access Without Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names attack surface: 'through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' No UC monitors for direct access to this boundary condition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor inbound connections to Splunk's PostgreSQL sidecar (identify port/interface from asset inventory). Alert on connections lacking proper Splunk session forwarding or authenticated trust. Flag any successful unauthenticated access attempts.

suggestion.title: Detect Arbitrary File Creation and Truncation via Splunk Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes post-compromise activity: 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is the attacker's impact goal (data destruction) but no UC was generated to detect it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk audit logs and filesystem logs for file creation, deletion, or truncation originating from unauthenticated sources or sidecar endpoints. Alert on unexpected modifications to sensitive paths (/etc, /opt/splunk, /var). Correlate with preceding endpoint access anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect Code Execution via Arbitrary File Write to Application Directories
suggestion.rationale: File-write primitives often enable RCE. Article's 'create arbitrary files' could precede execution if written to Splunk app directories or system hooks. No UC captures T1059 execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file writes to Splunk application directories (/opt/splunk/etc/apps, /opt/splunk/bin) via vulnerable endpoint. Inspect file content for script signatures (.sh, .py). Correlate with Splunk process spawning or abnormal command execution.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the direct attack vector and should trigger detection on any access to that service without valid authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar service (typically port 5432 or internal endpoint) for connection attempts lacking valid authentication credentials. Alert on any unauthenticated queries or connection strings from external/untrusted sources. Baseline known-good sidecar consumers and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Splunk Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the vulnerability enables attackers to 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Detection must monitor for file operations (CREATE, TRUNCATE, DROP) originating from the sidecar process or routed through it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CREATE/TRUNCATE/DROP file operations in PostgreSQL logs that either (a) are not from expected maintenance jobs, (b) target sensitive Splunk configuration or data files, or (c) originate from connections established without authentication. Look for calls to pg_file_* functions or similar dangerous PostgreSQL file I/O.

suggestion.title: Splunk Missing Authentication Bypass on Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly states 'Missing Authentication for Critical Function.' Any request to Splunk critical endpoints (likely including the sidecar) that bypasses authentication is the direct exploit pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag any HTTP requests to Splunk critical function endpoints (enumerate from documentation) that lack valid session tokens, API keys, or authentication headers. Splunk should require authentication; requests bypassing this are the vulnerability exploit.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Instance Asset Inventory with Patch Status Check
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry means active exploitation is occurring. Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and audit pressure. Enterprise must identify all Splunk instances exposed and cross-check patch dates against federal due-date 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Asset hunt: enumerate all Splunk Enterprise instances across your fleet via CMDB, network scanning, or vulnerability scanner. For each, check (a) version against CVE-2026-20253 advisory, (b) last patch date, (c) network exposure (internal vs. internet-facing). Instances not patched by 2026-06-21 should be escalated as critical.

suggestion.title: Rclone process spawning shell or scripting engine (exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly defines this detection (exploit phase, HIGH confidence) to catch post-exploitation command execution when inline remote config triggers initialization code. Pipeline failed to extract despite structured Splunk and Defender KQL rules provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (shell, scripting engines, curl, wget, LOLBins, mshta, wscript) spawned from rclone parent process. Filter for non-system accounts to reduce false positives from legitimate rclone automation.

suggestion.title: HTTP requests to rclone RC endpoint with inline-remote configuration pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article defines detection for delivery/initial access phase (HIGH confidence). Attack vector: unauthenticated GET/HEAD to /:remote:path patterns with inline config syntax. Pipeline failed to extract despite this being the direct exploitation mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET/HEAD requests to port 5572 with URL patterns: brackets+colons like [local:...] OR parameters exec=/command=. High baseline risk given unauthenticated exposure. Pair Defender endpoint signals with WAF/web gateway logs since endpoint visibility is limited to connection-level.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable rclone version (1.46.0 - 1.74.2) deployed on managed endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly provides inventory detection (HIGH confidence) to identify at-risk assets. Version range clearly defined: 1.46.0–1.74.2 vulnerable; >=1.55.0 enables RCE, <1.55.0 file-read-only. Foundational for patch prioritization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query asset inventory for rclone software with major=1, minor in [46..73], or (minor=74 AND patch<3). Bifurcate RCE-capable (>=1.55.0) from file-read-only versions for patch planning.

suggestion.title: Rclone RCD listener bound to non-localhost without HTTP authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article provides configuration-based detection (HIGH confidence) to flag vulnerable standing. Detects both explicit non-loopback binding via --rc-addr AND absence of authentication flags. Pipeline failed to extract despite structured rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rclone processes with --rc-serve but missing --rc-user, --rc-pass, or --rc-htpasswd. Flag if --rc-addr absent (vulnerable default) OR explicitly non-loopback. High-confidence misconfiguration indicator.

suggestion.title: HTTP authentication bypass attempt on rclone RC endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation via 'inline remote instantiation' that circumvents CVE-2026-41179 auth fix. Missing detection for HTTP request sequences where initial 401 response is followed by retry with modified parameters, indicating auth-layer bypass attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GET/HEAD to /:remote:path → 401/403 → GET with modified inline-remote parameters (different config) → 200 response. Sequence indicates attacker adapted payload to bypass authentication check.

suggestion.title: Network reconnaissance of rclone RC listener (port 5572 probing)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation beginning with unauthenticated requests, implying prior service discovery. Missing detection for attackers probing port 5572 to enumerate rclone RC service availability before exploitation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect network connections to TCP 5572 from unexpected external sources. Baseline legitimate RC client access, then alert on: rapid sequential probes (horizontal scanning), auth failures before successful exploitation, or connections from known scanning tool IPs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—direct indicator of initial access vector. Pipeline missed endpoint-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise hosts for unauthenticated HTTP/TCP access to PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or proxied variants). Flag successful connections from unexpected sources or without valid Splunk auth tokens. Baseline: who legitimately accesses this service.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Write/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies capability to 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—exploitation would manifest in filesystem operations. Pipeline generated no execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events originating from Splunk Enterprise sidecar service processes (splunk-postgresql or sidecar wrapper), especially to unexpected directories (/etc, system paths, application roots). Correlate with network connections to sidecar service from external sources.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'asset-exposure hunt' with template substitution for CVE detection. Pipeline failed to generate vulnerability-scanner-driven detection despite explicit instruction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner assets for Splunk Enterprise instances flagged with CVE-2026-20253. Cross-correlate with network exposure (public-facing, internet-routable). Prioritize federal agency scan by patch due date 2026-06-21.

suggestion.title: Authentication Bypass to File Manipulation Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'missing authentication for critical function'—core weakness is auth-bypass enabling subsequent file ops. Pipeline skipped credential-access / defense-evasion framing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Splunk sidecar endpoints that lack authentication headers or contain null/empty auth tokens, followed within seconds by file system modification events on the Splunk host. Alert on anomalous privilege escalation in service context.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug'—clear initial-access / exploitation event. Pipeline produced zero IOCs and zero kill-chain reconstruction, missing T1190 entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to /wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/ endpoints for signatures matching known CVEs in Gravity SMTP (version disclosure, unauthenticated config access, path traversal patterns). Alert if requests precede plugin update events on the same host.

suggestion.title: SMTP API Credential Exposure in Plugin Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Expose API Keys'—credential-access is the core threat. Pipeline failed to map T1552.001 or generate detections for credential disclosure via plugin settings/database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized read access to Gravity SMTP configuration (gravity_smtp_settings, plugin options table rows). Alert on exfiltration of base64-encoded or plaintext SMTP API keys. Flag if API credentials are logged, cached, or transmitted over unencrypted channels.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Email Relay via Compromised API Keys
suggestion.rationale: Exposing SMTP API keys enables attackers to abuse email relay for C2, phishing, spam—post-exploitation impact the pipeline completely missed despite this being the direct consequence of the credential exposure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate SMTP API key compromise timestamp with anomalous mail relay patterns: sudden spike in email volume from WordPress instance, emails sent to attacker-controlled domains, SMTP authentication from unexpected IPs using recovered credentials.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Gravity SMTP Plugin Installation Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline did not extract plugin name, version ranges, or CVE identifier needed for asset inventory control. Article headline 'Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin' should trigger version-specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate installed WordPress plugins via wp_options table, plugin directory scan, or WP-CLI enumeration. Extract gravity-smtp version. Alert on presence of versions ≤ [CVE-affected range]. Compare plugin versions against advisory baseline.

suggestion.title: First successful cross-realm alarm DELETE by authenticated user
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'An authenticated user in any realm can delete alarms belonging to other realms'—the *first* successful cross-realm delete is the smoking gun of exploitation. Pipeline missed baseline detection for initial breach of realm boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect a DELETE request to /api/{realm}/alarm that succeeds (200/204) where the authenticated user's home_realm does not match the target realm being queried. This requires joining Web logs with OpenRemote user-realm mappings to establish the user's authority boundary, then flagging cross-boundary DELETE operations.

suggestion.title: Alarm deletion from realm user has no membership in
suggestion.rationale: Core IDOR: 'the bulk removeAlarms() method only verifies that the caller's own realm is active and accessible, but never checks whether the targeted alarms belong to that realm.' Need correlation of deleted alarm IDs against realm ACLs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor OpenRemote application logs for DELETE operations on alarm entities where the requesting user's realm authorization does not include the alarm's parent realm. Requires parsing alarm metadata (realm field) from logs and cross-referencing against user_realm membership tables.

suggestion.title: Repeated alarm ID enumeration within single HTTP session
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must enumerate or guess valid alarm IDs across other realms. Article describes 'supplying arbitrary alarm IDs'—detection should catch patterns of rapid, sequential ID probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sessions that attempt DELETEs on 5+ distinct alarm IDs within a single realm within 2 minutes, where fewer than 2 actually exist (indicated by 404 or error response patterns in OpenRemote). This signals ID enumeration.

suggestion.title: IDOR privilege escalation: non-admin user deleting alarms outside base realm
suggestion.rationale: The IDOR grants delete capability beyond the user's authorized realm—this is privilege escalation via a broken authorization check. Pipeline assigned T1087 but missed T1548 (Abuse Elevation Control).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DELETE operations from users with base role != admin on alarms in realms where that user has no explicit membership or grant. Indicator of IDOR abuse escalating implicit privileges.

suggestion.title: Bulk alarm deletion after failed authorization attempts in other realm
suggestion.rationale: Attacker may probe /api/realm-X/alarm with failed auth, then if X's alarm DELETE endpoint is vulnerable, escalate to successful deletion. Combines UC_3_2 signal with successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In a 15-minute window, flag patterns where the same user generates 2+ 401/403 errors on DELETE /api/realm-X/alarm, followed by 3+ 200/204 responses to DELETE /api/realm-Y/alarm (where Y != user's home realm). Indicates probe-then-exploit against cross-realm IDOR.

suggestion.title: Explicit cosign verification failure followed by image pull success
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'could serve a correctly signed image for verification, then swap it with malicious content between verification and pull'—detection must catch explicit cosign API failures (wrong signature) that are ignored. Pipeline UC_7_3 is too vague.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Crossplane reconciliation logs for cosign verify commands that report verification failures or invalid signatures, immediately followed by successful image pulls of those same packages. TOCTOU assumes verification pass is recorded but pull pulls different content; catch where verification is attempted, fails or is bypassed, yet the package is still pulled and installed.

suggestion.title: ImageConfig verification disabled between package request and installation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attacker could modify ImageConfig to disable verification. Pipeline detects removal but misses the attack sequence: removal happens specifically when a mutable-tag package is pending installation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate K8s API events: detect when an ImageConfig verification policy is deleted or modified to remove cosign checks, and within 120 seconds, a Provider/Configuration using a mutable tag is created/updated in the same namespace. This captures the defender-evasion phase of the attack.

suggestion.title: OCI registry credentials or permissions used from anomalous sources during tag overwrite
suggestion.rationale: Article focuses on malicious registry serving different content per request. Pipeline UC_7_4 detects timing correlation but doesn't flag anomalous source identity. Detect when ECR PutImage/BatchPutImage originates from IP/principal not normally seen pushing to that repository.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build baseline of which IAM principals and source IPs push to Crossplane provider/configuration repositories. Alert when tag overwrites occur from anomalous principals or IPs, especially if they occur within seconds of Crossplane reconciliation events.

suggestion.title: Crossplane package reconciliation loop with repeated digest mismatches
suggestion.rationale: When TOCTOU exploit succeeds, Crossplane reconciler would pull mismatched content, fail validation, and retry. Pipeline doesn't detect the reconciliation failure pattern that indicates successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Crossplane Provider/Configuration reconciliation status for repeated failures due to digest mismatches (pull succeeds but content hash doesn't match expected). Cluster failures with mutable-tag packages getting pulled, failing validation, then re-pulled with different content indicates TOCTOU window exploitation.

suggestion.title: Rapid consecutive image pulls of same mutable tag with varying digests
suggestion.rationale: TOCTOU exploit involves pulling same tag twice in quick succession but getting different content. Pipeline UC_7_3 attempts this but with weak regex. Need explicit detection: same mutable tag, multiple pulls, multiple digests in kubelet/container logs within 30-60 second window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract image pull events from kubelet logs for mutable-tag references (no @sha256 digest). Group by tag, look for 2+ pulls of the same tag within 60 seconds from the same Crossplane pod. If different manifests/digests are pulled, flag as likely TOCTOU exploitation.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Gravity SMTP REST endpoint access attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Threat actors are exploiting an unauthenticated information disclosure vulnerability' with specific endpoint 'requests to '/wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data' found in web server access logs, particularly those including the '?page=gravitysmtp-settings' query parameter'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GET requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data with query parameter ?page=gravitysmtp-settings and HTTP 200 response, especially unauthenticated requests. Baseline: exploit spike was 4 million attempts on June 7 alone.

suggestion.title: Successful Gravity SMTP system report exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allowed unauthenticated GET requests to receive a comprehensive JSON "System Report"' containing 'API keys, secrets, and OAuth tokens for configured email integrations, credentials for third-party email services, WordPress configuration details, server and PHP environment information, database configuration details'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP responses from /wp-json/gravitysmtp/v1/tests/mock-data with large response body (200+ bytes) containing JSON fields referencing 'key', 'secret', 'token', 'password', or 'credential'. Response content should include AWS SES, Google, Mailjet, Resend, or Zoho service identifiers.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP vulnerable plugin version installed
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'affects all versions of the plugin from 2.1.4 and older' and 'has been addressed in version 2.1.5, released on March 17'. Active on 100,000 sites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation or continued presence of Gravity SMTP plugin versions ≤2.1.4 via WordPress REST API query /wp-json/plugins endpoint, or via web server logs showing activation, or via file system scanning. Flag if version < 2.1.5 and exploitation attempts are visible in access logs.

suggestion.title: Email service credential abuse via stolen Gravity SMTP credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exposure of live third-party API credentials means an attacker could abuse the site's connected email services, while...This allows an attacker to impersonate the victim to third parties'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor AWS SES, Google Workspace, Mailjet, Resend, and Zoho API logs for access patterns anomalous to the WordPress site's known behavior: unusual IP addresses, unexpected geographic origin, API key first-use, bulk email sending, credential creation, or account modifications.

suggestion.title: WordPress reconnaissance via Gravity SMTP information disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'detailed system report significantly lowers the effort required to plan further attacks' and exposes 'installed plugins, themes, and software versions, server and PHP environment information, database...server version and table names'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful Gravity SMTP endpoint responses (200 status with JSON system report) with subsequent exploit attempts against the enumerated plugins, themes, or server software within 24-72 hours. Flag if the same source IP exploits the SMTP endpoint then targets other known vulnerabilities matching the disclosed versions.

suggestion.title: Mass Gravity SMTP exploitation campaign detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Wordfence firewall has blocked more than 17 million attempts against protected customers' and 'Exploitation activity spiked on June 7, with 4 million requests being blocked that day'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained spike in requests to /wp-json/gravitysmtp endpoints from multiple source IPs (distributed scanning) or single IP with high request rate (4M+ per day). Baseline: June 7 2026 saw 4M blocked attempts globally. Tuning: filter to site's normal traffic volume + 200%.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise PostgreSQL Sidecar Unauthenticated Access Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — the core attack path. Pipeline generated no detection use case for this explicit exploitation technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/network requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint (port 5432 or service proxy) that successfully execute file operations (POST/PUT with truncate/create payloads) without preceding authentication challenge or valid auth token. Correlate timing with known CVE-2026-20253 exploitation attempts.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation Impact on Splunk Backend
suggestion.rationale: Attack outcome stated as 'create or truncate arbitrary files' — represents destructive impact phase (T1485/T1561). Pipeline missed this impact detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk Enterprise backend processes (uid=splunk) for unexpected file truncation (size→0) or creation in critical directories ($SPLUNK_HOME/etc, /var/log, database paths). Flag files modified without corresponding administrative audit entries or configuration deployment events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure and Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires fleet asset-exposure hunting. Article specifies federal patch due-date 2026-06-21 and notes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Pipeline output contains zero asset-inventory or scanning-based use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all vulnerability scans for Splunk Enterprise instances matching pre-2026-06-21 patch dates or affected versions. Cross-reference CMDB for network exposure (internet-facing vs. internal-only). Generate compliance report for federal agencies against 2026-06-21 remediation deadline.

suggestion.title: REST API Missing-Authentication Detection on Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause explicitly 'missing authentication for critical function.' Pipeline did not generate probing/enumeration detection for unauthenticated API access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline Splunk REST API calls that should require authentication. Alert when critical endpoints (/services/admin/*, /services/data/*, /services/saved/searches) are accessed without X-Auth-Token or session cookie, or return successful responses (200/201) where 401 Unauthorized is expected. Correlate unauthenticated file-operation calls (POST with `truncate=1` or `create=true` parameters).

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure Hunt – Splunk Enterprise Internet-Accessible Instances

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Detections Without Patch Compliance
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability is actively exploited (CISA KEV status) with federal patch due date 2026-06-21. Detection should flag scanner hits paired with age-of-patch metadata.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner detecting CVE-2026-20253 in Splunk Enterprise. Cross-reference with patch inventory; prioritize instances running versions published before the 2026-06-18 disclosure date. Escalate if instance is internet-routable.

suggestion.title: Joomla JCE Plugin RCE Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'actively exploited'—pipeline generated zero detection use cases. JCE vulnerabilities are exploited via HTTP requests to plugin endpoints; article directly establishes this attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to Joomla JCE plugin paths (/media/jce/*, /plugins/editors/jce/*) containing parameter payloads with PHP execution patterns (eval, system, exec, backtick operators, base64_decode, assert), especially from untrusted sources or anomalous user agents.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies outcome: 'PHP Code Execution.' Pipeline should detect exec spawned by PHP interpreter or web server process. Core detection for post-exploitation validation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child process creation from php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or web server processes (apache2, nginx, w3wp.exe) executing system commands (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, powershell.exe) with arguments indicating reverse shells, data exfil, or reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Persistence via JCE File Upload
suggestion.rationale: JCE RCE flaw enables arbitrary file write to web-accessible directories. Pipeline should detect executable file creation post-exploitation for persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Joomla installation directories for creation of .php, .php5, .phtml files with timestamps correlating to exploit activity, especially in /media/, /plugins/, or /components/ paths with suspicious content (obfuscated code, base64 payloads, eval calls).

suggestion.title: CVE-Specific Vulnerability Scanning Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article references active exploitation but pipeline extracted no CVE ID or version indicators. Vulnerability scanners and PoC tools have known signatures for this flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect version-discovery probes and vulnerability scanner requests targeting Joomla JCE plugin endpoints (e.g., requests to known-vulnerable plugin manifest or version disclosure endpoints), and PoC script behaviors (multi-stage payloads, specific parameter fuzzing patterns).

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Unauthenticated Critical-Function Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' Pipeline missed the initial-access detection pattern entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise endpoints (especially /_sidecar/* or PostgreSQL-sidecar-related paths) that succeed (HTTP 200/201) without prior authentication token/session context. Flag requests originating from untrusted networks reaching default Splunk ports (8000, 8089).

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files' — this is the impact phase. Pipeline failed to suggest impact-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, modification, or deletion operations initiated by Splunk sidecar child processes (e.g., spawned from splunkd or PostgreSQL sidecar handlers) when correlating with HTTP 200/201 responses on sidecar endpoints. Escalate if truncation targets system-critical paths (configs, binaries, logs).

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'even if scanners say not vulnerable...it's worth one quick check across your fleet' and references asset-exposure hunt. Pipeline did not surface inventory/exposure detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan firewall/proxy logs for external (non-RFC1918) source IPs reaching Splunk Enterprise web-UI ports (8000, 8089, 9997) or any _sidecar/* endpoints. Cross-reference against asset inventory and identify Splunk instances unintentionally exposed to the internet or reachable without VPN context.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Scanner Hits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-20253. Pipeline failed to suggest scanner-output detection and alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner report (Nessus, Qualys, Tenable, etc.) detecting CVE-2026-20253 on any asset. Escalate to critical if (a) the affected Splunk instance is internet-reachable, (b) remediation is past the federal due date (2026-06-21), or (c) the system handles sensitive data.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated HTTP Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—detecting requests to the sidecar without auth tokens is the initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically :8191 or dynamically discovered) from external sources without valid Splunk authentication tokens. Alert on successful responses (200/201) to unauthenticated requests.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names the exploitation action: 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—post-compromise detection of file I/O operations triggered by or originating from the sidecar daemon.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or deletion events where the parent/initiator is the PostgreSQL sidecar process or requests proxied through it. Flag truncations of critical system/config files, especially correlated with prior unauthenticated HTTP access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Vulnerability Presence Check
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes CISA KEV status and federal remediation due date (2026-06-21)—standard vulnerability scanning for this CVE ID across the Splunk fleet is the canonical hunt pattern referenced in the article itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for CVE-2026-20253 matches. Cross-check against actual Splunk Enterprise versions deployed; reconcile false negatives (scanner cleared, version actually vulnerable) to find untracked or misreported instances.

suggestion.title: Network Reconnaissance of Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Ports
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies the attack surface is the 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—network-level detection of port scans or connection attempts to typical sidecar ports from untrusted sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on successful or attempted connections to Splunk sidecar service ports from external IP ranges, especially with high request volume or abnormal payloads. Track failed authentication attempts followed by exploitation.

suggestion.title: Inline remote configuration syntax in HTTP requests to rclone RC
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Inline remote configuration can set backend options that execute local commands during initialization' but no detection specifically hunts for this payload in HTTP request bodies/paths. The attack pattern includes square-bracket syntax like '[local:exec=', '[[:option=', or unencoded backend option injection. This is distinct from connection-level signals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP GET/HEAD requests to rclone RC endpoint where URL path contains inline remote brackets with option injection: patterns like [local:exec=, [[:command=, or URL-encoded variants %5B%5B. This represents the actual command-injection payload. Requires HTTP proxy/WAF or rclone HTTP logging visibility; network layer alone insufficient.

suggestion.title: Rclone configuration file containing inline remote definitions
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions inline remote configuration as attack vector. Legitimate rclone config files (~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf or %APPDATA%\rclone\rclone.conf) containing '[remotes]' with inline backend definitions (especially exec, local, or system-interaction backends) signal either attacker persistence or pre-staged exploitation setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rclone config file creation or modification where content contains '[' + ':' inline remote syntax, particularly with exec=, command=, or local= directives. High-fidelity when paired with HTTP request detection (UC_103_2 supplement) or suspicious process spawning (UC_103_1).

suggestion.title: Port 5572 listeners on hosts without expected rclone deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article references port 5572 as the rclone RC default endpoint. Unexpected listeners on this port (or inferred via process-to-port binding) on hosts where rclone is not in asset inventory indicate either new attacker-deployed instances or missed asset data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unexpected port 5572 listeners (via network monitoring or command-line auditing) against rclone asset inventory (UC_103_3). Flag new listeners on this port as potential attacker-deployed instances or reconnaissance targets. Combine with user context to identify privilege abuse.

suggestion.title: Failed or successful authentications to rclone RC endpoint without credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'unauthenticated' access. If rclone RC logs are available, detect requests missing HTTP Authorization headers, Bearer tokens, or Basic auth credentials—especially followed by command-execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor rclone RC access logs or HTTP proxy logs for GET/HEAD requests to /[*:*]/* or similar inline-remote paths where Authorization header is absent AND subsequent process activity spawns shell/script interpreter. Requires rclone logging or HTTP-layer visibility; network flow data insufficient.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — this is the primary attack vector; unauthorized access attempts must be detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk Enterprise sidecar endpoints lacking valid authentication credentials. Establish baseline of legitimate internal sidecar traffic; flag connections from external IPs or anomalous access patterns.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Arbitrary File Create/Truncate by Sidecar Service
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exploitation creates or truncates arbitrary files — file system activity during exploitation must be monitorable through process and file events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file creation or truncation by Splunk processes, especially in PostgreSQL directories or system paths. Correlate with authentication gaps to confirm unauthenticated exploitation.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Active Exploitation Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV entry explicitly indicates 'observed exploited in the wild' — CVE-specific detection is mandatory with federal patch due 2026-06-21.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for CVE-2026-20253 exploitation signatures against Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference vulnerability scanner output; flag unpatched instances with patch deadline passed.

suggestion.title: Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Service Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Article implies sidecar reachable without proper auth — service exposure and anomalous connection patterns indicate exploitation risk or active compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate connections to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar from authorized internal sources. Alert on external IP connections, non-standard ports, or incomplete authentication handshakes.

suggestion.title: Gravity SMTP Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names plugin and exploitation; attack vector not captured by pipeline. Article phrase: 'Hackers Exploit Gravity SMTP WordPress Plugin Bug'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests targeting Gravity SMTP plugin files (wp-content/plugins/gravity-smtp/) with payloads characteristic of CVE exploitation. Baseline expected plugin file access; alert on requests with suspicious parameters, injection attempts, or unusual HTTP methods targeting admin/settings endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized API Key Extraction from Plugin Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Impact stated as 'API Keys exposed' — this is a credential_access event. Pipeline did not map exposure mechanism to MITRE phase. Article phrase: 'Expose API Keys'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on direct queries to wp_options table for gravity-smtp options, or file reads of Gravity SMTP config files outside normal plugin lifecycle. Correlate with failed authorization or suspicious user contexts. Exfiltration: monitor for bulk export of wp_options or config file contents via POST/wget.

suggestion.title: WordPress Plugin File Anomaly — Gravity SMTP Unauthorized Modification
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation typically requires malicious payload delivery or config tampering. Article describes bug exploitation, implying unauthorized modification of plugin behavior or files. No defensive indicators captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Gravity SMTP plugin directory for modifications outside package manager or update workflows. Hash changes, new files, permission changes on .php files should be alerted. Baseline clean plugin hash and trigger on deviations.

suggestion.title: Compromised SMTP Credentials — Unauthorized Email Relay Activity
suggestion.rationale: API key exposure enables account compromise; pipeline missed impact phase detection. Exposed SMTP credentials lead to email spoofing/relay abuse. Article phrase: 'Expose API Keys' implies downstream email infra compromise.
log_sources: Email system audit logs (abnormal mail volume/recipients)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SMTP authentication from Gravity SMTP plugin using credentials associated with exploitation timeline. Monitor for: spike in mail volume, unusual recipients, geographic anomalies in relay source, authentication failure patterns preceding success. Cross-correlate plugin exploitation timestamp with SMTP anomalies.

suggestion.title: API Credential Enumeration via WordPress Database Access
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline did not model discovery/credential enumeration phase preceding exfiltration. WordPress DB contains plaintext or weakly-encrypted plugin credentials.
log_sources: File reads of wp-config.php or plugin config directories
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for WordPress admin account usage to access plugin settings pages or database queries selecting gravity-smtp option keys. Correlate with successful authentication via vulnerability vector (non-standard HTTP patterns, plugin RCE indicators). Baseline normal admin configuration review and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: API Key Leakage via WordPress Logs or Backups
suggestion.rationale: Gravity SMTP stores API keys in configuration; if plugin bug exposes serialized data or logs, keys leak. Pipeline did not address data exfiltration from plugin config stores.
log_sources: Error logs (plugin errors may expose config)
HTTP response inspection (error pages with leaked keys)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP responses containing API key-like strings (pattern: long alphanumeric tokens typical of SMTP/email API keys). Review WordPress debug logs for Gravity SMTP errors containing configuration data. Alert on unauthorized backup file access or exposure via web-accessible backup directories.

suggestion.title: Langflow HTTP request parameter injection - symlink traversal pattern (CVE-2026-55447 initial exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'symlink RCE' and 'symlink-traversal' as the attack vector but no UC hunts the web request or API call that injects the malicious path. Article phrase: 'BaseFileComponent symlink RCE' describes the vulnerability mechanism but existing UCs focus on post-exploitation (file read, RCE execution), not the injection itself.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Langflow endpoints (/api/v1/flows, /flows/{id}/run, component execution paths) for path traversal indicators in parameters: ../, ..\, symlink references, or absolute paths to /etc, /.ssh, /.aws. Flag requests from unauthenticated or external origins with file_path, input_path, or upload parameters containing traversal syntax.

suggestion.title: Symlink creation in Langflow working directory (CVE-2026-55447 attack staging)
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly depends on symlink traversal, but no UC detects symlink artifact creation. UC_5_1 hunts for a specific temporary file (/tmp/trip.docx) post-exploitation but misses the symlink setup phase. Article phrase: 'symlink-traversal' is the core mechanism but detection logic stops at file access, not symlink creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect symlink creation events (ln -s, CreateSymbolicLink, os.symlink) in /tmp, /var/tmp, or Langflow app directories by python, uvicorn, or gunicorn processes. Prioritize symlinks targeting credential paths (/.ssh/, /.aws/, /.kube/, /root) or system files (/etc/shadow, /etc/passwd). Correlate with subsequent file read events.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Langflow component instantiation with file parameters (CVE-2026-55447 workflow attack setup)
suggestion.rationale: Article names six vulnerable component types (Docling, FileComponent, VideoFileComponent, DoclingRemoteComponent, NvidiaIngestComponent, UnstructuredComponent) but no UC detects their creation or configuration with suspicious parameters. Attack requires first constructing a workflow graph with these components before symlink traversal can occur.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Langflow API calls to /graphs or /flows endpoints for POST/PUT payloads containing FileComponent, VideoFileComponent, UnstructuredComponent, DoclingRemoteComponent with file_path or input_path parameters containing ../, absolute paths, or env variable expansion (e.g., $HOME, $ROOT). Correlate with subsequent execution by Python interpreter.

suggestion.title: Python code execution from file parameters in Langflow context (CVE-2026-55447 RCE execution gap)
suggestion.rationale: UC_5_4 detects shell spawning (bash, sh) as post-RCE evidence but not the Python eval/exec that enabled it. Article states 'Python Interpreter RCE' (T1059.006) but the gap between parameter injection and shell invocation (where the initial Python code exec occurs) is unmonitored. Article phrase: 'Command and Scripting Interpreter: Python' indicates code execution but UC focuses on child processes, not the initial eval.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect eval(), exec(), or __import__() syscalls within Python worker processes (uvicorn, gunicorn, langflow-worker) where the code argument originates from deserialized user input (JSON payloads, file contents from file_path parameters). Look for frame patterns of exec() with compile() called on untrusted input, followed by network or shell spawning.

suggestion.title: Crossplane cosign signature verification timestamp mismatch (TOCTOU detection)
suggestion.rationale: Article core mechanic: 'malicious OCI registry could serve a correctly signed image for verification, then serve unverified content on pull.' No detection targets the timing anomaly—gap between when cosign verify succeeds and when image pull completes. Detectable via registry audit logs or cluster audit showing verify then different pull.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track cosign verify success timestamps and subsequent image pull operations. Flag when the same package reference (tag) is verified at time T1 but a different content hash is pulled at time T2 > T1 from the same registry, indicating potential race-condition exploitation.

suggestion.title: OCI registry endpoint substitution or hostname deviation in package reference
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation requires either compromising the registry or performing MitM to serve different content during verify vs. pull phases. Article mentions 'malicious OCI registry' but no detection looks for lateral movement to registry infrastructure or URL rewriting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package resource specs for registry hostname changes between successive deployments. Flag if pull_secret credentials are updated to point to a different OCI registry, or if DNS resolution for the registry FQDN changes to unexpected IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Cosign installation or cosign binary removal from cluster nodes
suggestion.rationale: Bypassing signature verification can be achieved by removing or disabling cosign itself on nodes. Article discusses signature verification mechanism but no detection explicitly monitors for cosign binary tampering or removal, which is a prerequisite attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect removal or modification of cosign binary paths (/usr/local/bin/cosign, container image registries' cosign sidecar) or execution of package install commands with environment variables that disable signature verification (e.g., COSIGN_SKIP_VERIFICATION=1).

suggestion.title: Multiple failed cosign verification attempts followed by successful package install
suggestion.rationale: An attacker might probe the signature verification mechanism, encounter failures, then disable it. Article does not explicitly call this out, but sequential failed-verify → disabled-verify → successful-install is a strong behavioral indicator of exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed cosign verification attempts (from logs or API errors) with subsequent successful package installations from the same user/service account within a narrow time window, paired with ImageConfig modifications that disable verification.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—attack vector not converted to detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP requests to Splunk PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint lacking authentication credentials or Authorization headers. Correlate unauthenticated POST/PUT/DELETE requests with subsequent unexpected file system modifications.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article core impact: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—impact phase completely absent from use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation by Splunk processes outside scheduled maintenance windows. Alert on unexpected writes to system-critical directories (/etc, /opt/splunk/etc) preceded by unauthenticated endpoint requests.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Splunk Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'CISA KEV entry...actively exploited in the wild' with federal remediation deadline 2026-06-21; asset-exposure hunt templates referenced but never instantiated.

Cross-reference vulnerability scanner results with network telemetry to identify internet-facing instances. Correlate scan findings with exploitation indicators (unauthenticated sidecar access logs).

suggestion.title: Missing Authentication Enforcement on Splunk Critical Functions
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is 'missing authentication for critical function'—no detection for auth-bypass or privilege-escalation-by-omission scenarios generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk API/endpoint audit logs for critical operations (file creation, deletion) lacking corresponding user authentication events. Alert on requests to sidecar endpoints returning success (2xx) without prior login event.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Internet Exposure – Asset Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'observed exploited in the wild' under CISA KEV and explicitly invokes T1190 (Exploit Public-Facing Application). Exploitation only viable if Splunk Enterprise ports (8089, 8000, 8191) are reachable from untrusted networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate internal Splunk Enterprise instances with listening ports 8000, 8089, 8191. Cross-reference against asset inventory with internet-routing paths. Flag any listening on internet-facing IPs or behind reverse proxies without WAF/authentication proxy.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Requests to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unauthenticated user' accessing 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' as the attack vector. Sidecar typically listens on high ephemeral or reserved ports behind Splunk; requests without auth headers or valid session tokens are anomalous.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Splunk access logs for requests to sidecar-related paths (e.g., /services/sidecar, /pgsql, /_postgres) lacking Authorization headers or valid session cookies. Correlate with failed auth attempts or 403→200 status progression.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Sidecar File Operation Anomalies – Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability allows 'create or truncate arbitrary files through [sidecar] endpoint'. Successful exploitation will manifest as file creation/deletion events, likely originating from Splunk service account or PostgreSQL process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation or truncation events where parent process is Splunk Enterprise or PostgreSQL sidecar, targeting directories outside Splunk's application/data/etc/index directories (e.g., /etc, /var, /tmp with suspicious patterns, user home dirs). Flag rapid truncation of existing files.

suggestion.title: Splunk Service Port Scanning & Enumeration – Pre-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates active exploitation. Reconnaissance phase precedes exploitation; attackers scan for open Splunk ports and probe endpoints for authentication requirements before triggering CVE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect external source IPs scanning Splunk ports (8000, 8089, 8191) across multiple targets in close time window. Look for GET/HEAD requests to common Splunk endpoints (e.g., /services/auth/login, /api/apps) returning 401/403, followed by attempts to /services/sidecar or PostgreSQL endpoints.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Version Detection – Known Vulnerable Versions
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-20253 affects specific Splunk Enterprise versions. Asset inventory should tag instances against affected version matrix to prioritize patching by patch-due date (2026-06-21).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Splunk cluster master / deployment client logs for version strings, or API-enumerate /services/server/info endpoints. Cross-ref against Splunk security advisory CVE-2026-20253 affected versions. Flag instances not yet patched to remediated version by federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via PostgreSQL Sidecar Query Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes file creation capability; implicit risk is that truncated or created files could contain exfiltrated data. PostgreSQL sidecar abuse could enable data queries or file reads before exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL sidecar query logs (if enabled) for unusual SELECT statements on sensitive tables or volumes. Correlate with outbound network connections from Splunk service IP. Flag data dumps to temp files followed by network transfer.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar — Unauthenticated Access Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow an unauthenticated user' to exploit via 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — core attack vector requiring asset-exposure hunt for reachable Splunk services per template instructions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for unauthenticated HTTP/HTTPS requests to Splunk ports (8089, 8088, or sidecar-specific) originating externally. Flag successful connections without prior authentication that precede file operations; correlate with connection logs + file events.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Creation/Truncation via Splunk Sidecar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Exploit payload: 'create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint' — direct execution impact requiring file-event detection keyed to Splunk service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file creation or truncation events initiated by Splunk service account (splunkd process) to unexpected system/config/audit directories. Prioritize truncations of log files; correlate with unauthenticated network access within 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Splunk Instance Inventory — PostgreSQL Sidecar Exposure Assessment
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV implies active exploitation; federal patch due 2026-06-21 necessitates rapid inventory of affected instances. Article emphasizes asset-exposure hunt as canonical detection; must identify which Splunk deployments expose sidecar.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner, CMDB, and cloud-security tools for Splunk Enterprise instances with version ≤ patched threshold and network-reachable PostgreSQL sidecar ports (5432 or Splunk-specific). Cross-check inbound firewall rules permitting external access.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'unauthenticated user can create or truncate arbitrary files' and CISA KEV means active wild exploitation. Recommended hunt template references asset-exposure pattern; this is the canonical first detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search Splunk instances for inbound requests to PostgreSQL sidecar endpoint on port 5432 or documented service path from unauthenticated IPs. Correlate with vulnerability scanner data for CVE-2026-20253 detection flags. High-confidence signal if combined with failed authentication logs.

suggestion.title: Splunk Missing Authentication Bypass — Sidecar Endpoint Access
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint.' This is the vulnerability itself; detect direct requests to service endpoint bypassing Splunk auth.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to /_internal or PostgreSQL sidecar endpoints (unpatched Splunk instances) that lack X-Splunk-Authorization headers or session tokens. Flag if source is external/untrusted network.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Create/Truncate via Splunk PostgreSQL Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'create or truncate arbitrary files.' This is impact behavior distinct from exploitation; detect file operations post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Splunk Service Endpoint Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in 'PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—attackers must first locate/probe the service. Detect reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for repetitive HTTP/TCP connections to Splunk instance ports (8089, 8000) followed by requests to non-standard paths (/services, /_internal, /api/services) from single source without valid auth, especially from external IP ranges.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-20253 Patch Deployment & Compliance Verification
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV federal due-date 2026-06-21 mentioned; article states 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Verify deployed patches and version compliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Splunk Enterprise instances for version >= patched release. Flag instances running pre-patch versions after 2026-06-21 deadline. Cross-ref against CMDB for inventory accuracy.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Access to Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability allows 'unauthenticated user to create or truncate arbitrary files through a PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoint'—sidecar accessibility is the entry point and central to the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS traffic to Splunk instances on PostgreSQL-related ports or sidecar service paths from untrusted networks. Alert on requests lacking Splunk authentication headers or bypass patterns targeting /services or /api endpoints on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary File Manipulation via Splunk PostgreSQL Sidecar
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attacker can 'create or truncate arbitrary files'—post-exploitation file operations are the impact mechanism and directly detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file creation, truncation, or deletion operations originating from Splunk sidecar processes or PostgreSQL service accounts. Prioritize audit log, config file, and license file modifications; flag bulk deletions in var/log or similar.

suggestion.title: Exposed Splunk Enterprise Service Endpoint Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Exploit requires sidecar accessibility from untrusted network. Article context implies exposed admin/service ports are the attack surface; asset exposure is the prerequisite vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan for Splunk Enterprise instances with exposed PostgreSQL sidecar ports (typically 5432 or custom service ports) reachable from external networks. Flag any unauthenticated service endpoints or missing firewall rules blocking non-admin access.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Vulnerable Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: CISA KEV requires asset inventory against patch baseline. Article specifies CVE-2026-20253 and federal due date 2026-06-21; unpatched Splunk instances are the vulnerable population.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner or Splunk version inventory to identify unpatched Splunk Enterprise instances. Cross-reference CVE-2026-20253 against installed versions and flag those not meeting federal patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Splunk Enterprise Asset Exposure – CVE-2026-20253
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to asset-exposure hunt template and emphasizes 'KEV implies active exploitation against exposed assets'; no UC generated despite this being the foundational detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query inventory for Splunk Enterprise instances externally accessible on ports 8000, 8089, 8191 and PostgreSQL sidecar service endpoints.
